They rushed toward Leon and Celeste with weapons drawn.
They planned to overwhelm them with numbers.
But Leon didn’t move.
Dozens of players rushed toward him.
And yet...
He simply watched them calmly.
Compared to the battles he had experienced in his previous life...
This felt almost pathetic.
When he had fought the servants of the [God of Eternity], the battlefield had been far more terrifying.
Still...
Leon knew he couldn’t keep comparing everything to the past.
Many of the players around looked confident.
After all, CarLover58 himself was quite strong.
[ID: CarLover58]
[Level: 73]
[Talent: ???]
[Skills: ???]
[Combat Power: ???]
CarLover58 laughed loudly as he approached.
"My [Combat Power] is above 350,000!" he shouted proudly.
"You’re finished!"
Several other strong players followed behind him.
Most of them were above level 70.
Under normal circumstances, a group like this would dominate the battlefield.
CarLover58 himself belonged to the human race and had clearly invested heavily in combat abilities.
He truly was strong.
But unfortunately for him...
He was facing Leon.
SLASH!
Leon’s sword moved faster than anyone could follow.
The blade flashed once.
CarLover58’s twin swords shattered instantly.
The [Blood Heart Blessing] of Leon’s [Power Sword] doubled his [Strength] after all.
The moment their weapons collided, the difference in strength was obvious.
CarLover58’s eyes widened.
Then—
His head separated from his body.
The kill happened so quickly that many players didn’t even realize what had happened at first.
CarLover58’s body collapsed to the ground.
And Leon had already moved on.
The rest of the charging players were only seconds away now.
Leon raised his sword again.
Crescent Slash!
He gathered power into the blade for a brief moment before swinging forward.
Fwoosh!
A massive crescent-shaped wave of energy shot forward.
Several players attempted to block the attack.
Some raised shields.
Others tried using defensive skills.
None of it worked.
The crescent slash tore straight through them.
Bodies split apart.
Armor shattered.
Several players were cut in half instantly.
Leon watched the result with mild curiosity.
’Interesting...
I guess the [Power Sword]’s blessing also affects attacks like this.’
Technically, [Crescent Slash] was a ranged ability.
But the attack still originated from his sword.
Which meant the blessing of the weapon enhanced its power as well.
That was good to know.
Meanwhile, the situation on Celeste’s side was just as violent.
Torrent of Flames!
Pyra unleashed her only offensive ability once again.
A massive pillar of flames erupted from the ground.
Players caught in the attack screamed as the fire engulfed them.
Some players tried attacking Pyra directly after seeing her ability.
But Celeste immediately moved to defend her.
Ember Ball!
Celeste raised one hand.
A glowing sphere of flames formed instantly.
The fire came directly from the [Phoenix Ember] connected to her talent.
She threw the sphere into a nearby group of players.
Boom!
The explosion sent several players flying across the battlefield.
And she wasn’t finished yet.
Flame Clone!
Fwoosh!
A second Celeste suddenly appeared beside her.
The copy looked exactly like her, but its entire body was made of fire.
"Kill them," Celeste ordered calmly.
The clone immediately rushed forward.
Leon watched the ability while continuing to fight.
This was actually the first time he had seen most of Celeste’s abilities in action.
The flaming clone dashed toward a group of players and began attacking with its spear.
Stab!
Slash!
Kick!
Several players were struck down quickly.
At the same time, Leon raised his staff.
And he activated another ability: [Advanced Necromancy].
Dark energy spread across the ground.
Then—
Crack!
Crack!
Bones burst out of the earth.
Twenty-five skeletons slowly rose from the ground.
Fifteen of them were [Undead Skeletons].
The other ten were [Undead Mage].
The skeleton warriors carried rusted swords in their hands.
The undead mages wore small robes and held staffs.
Leon observed them with satisfaction.
’Nice.’
His current [Combat Power] had reached around 420,000.
Because of that, each of his summoned skeletons possessed roughly 250,000 Combat Power.
That meant many of them were stronger than the players trying to fight them.
’This is the real power of necromancy,’ Leon thought, ’As long as I grow stronger... so do my summons.’
He paid little attention to the normal skeletons.
Instead, he focused on the [Undead Mage] as they were the new addition.
Several players rushed toward them, hoping to destroy the weaker-looking summons.
The skeleton mages lifted their staffs.
Fireball!
Ten blazing fireballs shot through the air simultaneously.
Boom!
Explosions erupted across the battlefield.
Players were blasted apart instantly.
Leon nodded in satisfaction.
’Just like I expected.’
The undead mages were extremely effective.
And with that...
The battle completely collapsed.
What had started as a massive alliance quickly turned into pure panic.
Leon, Celeste and their summons.
Together, they carved through the battlefield like a storm.
Players fell one after another.
Eventually, many of them realized the truth: they had no chance.
Several players began running away.
But escape was impossible.
Slash!
The [Undead Skeletons] chased down anyone attempting to flee.
Their movements were relentless and efficient.
One by one, the remaining players were hunted down.
The massacre continued for nearly twenty minutes.
Until finally...
Silence returned to the battlefield.
Every single player around them had disappeared.
Celeste exhaled slowly.
"We must have killed at least a thousand players," she said with a small grin.
"Feels... good."
Leon glanced at the event counter.
[Players Left: 5,639]
He nodded, "Not much left now."
He opened the ranking window briefly.
His position remained unchanged: first place.
And the gap between him and the others had grown even larger.
Since the kills made by his skeletons also counted toward his score, his point total had increased rapidly during the battle.
Leon closed the window.
A small smile appeared on his face.
It seemed like this event...
Was going far smoother than he had originally expected.

chapters.title: Chapter 163: The Divine Academy’s Examination Event [4]
paragraphs: Ding!
[You are currently in first place with 2,029 Points.]
Leon glanced at the ranking window floating in front of him and smiled slightly.
His score had crossed the two-thousand mark after the massive battle they had just fought.
Celeste wasn’t far behind either.
She was now sitting in second place with 1,547 points.
For comparison, the player in third place only had 1,045 points.
The gap between them was enormous.
At this stage of the event, catching up to Leon or Celeste would be almost impossible.
Even if someone managed to kill several players quickly, the difference in points was simply too large.
Leon closed the ranking window.
"Let’s keep going," he said with a grin. "At this point we could probably sit around and do nothing and still win... but let’s not risk it."
Celeste nodded without hesitation. She clearly didn’t mind continuing the hunt.
The thrill of battle still lingered in her eyes after the fight they had just finished.
Without wasting any time, the two of them began moving again, searching for any remaining players nearby.
A few minutes later—
Ding!
[Only 5,000 Players remain.]
Leon whistled softly.
"Damn."
The event had entered its final stage.
However, things would slow down from this point onward.
Earlier, players had constantly run into each other because there were so many participants.
Now that the number had dropped so much, finding enemies would become harder.
Many players would also start hiding to survive longer.
Leon looked ahead and then pointed forward.
"Go," he ordered calmly, the twenty-five skeletons he had summoned immediately reacted, "Kill anyone you find."
The skeletons spread out across the area like a small hunting squad.
Leon smiled slightly while watching them leave.
Having twenty-five summons was almost like commanding a small army.
Even if some of them were destroyed, it didn’t really matter. They could simply respawn after one minute.
Meanwhile, Celeste had her own way of searching for enemies.
She turned toward the small phoenix resting on her shoulder.
"Pyra," she said calmly. "Use [Flame Sense]."
The small phoenix chirped in response.
A moment later, its body burst into brighter flames.
Fwoosh!
Pyra shot into the air like a streak of fire.
Leon raised an eyebrow. Celeste noticed his interest and explained.
"[Flame Sense] allows Pyra to detect people by sensing the heat coming from their bodies," she said. "It means no one can really hide from us."
Leon blinked in surprise, "Damn."
That ability was extremely useful.
Even players hiding underground or behind obstacles could still be detected if their body heat gave them away.
Leon quickly thought about how to use that advantage. Then he smiled.
"Let’s head back to the [Canyon of Death]," he said. "Anyone who survived this long by hiding is probably there."
He paused for a moment before adding,
"And after that... we’ll go to the [Citadel of Dusk]."
Celeste nodded. The two of them began running toward the canyon.
Along the way, they encountered two unlucky players who were attempting to travel quietly through the plains.
Neither of them survived more than a few seconds.
Eventually, after several minutes of running, Leon and Celeste arrived at the edge of the canyon once again.
The massive cliffs stretched downward into darkness.
Celeste looked toward Pyra, "Try again.
The phoenix hovered in the air and activated [Flame Sense] once more.
A few seconds passed. Then Celeste grinned.
"Found some." She looked toward Leon, "Do you want to...?"
Leon shook his head slightly, "You can go," he said.
"My position is basically guaranteed now," he explained. "Right now the goal is making sure you keep second place."
Celeste smiled, "Alright."
Leon still ordered several skeletons to accompany her.
Even if she was strong, having extra help never hurt.
Without another word, Celeste jumped down into the canyon.
The skeletons followed her immediately. They disappeared into the darkness below.
Leon stayed above the canyon, watching the surroundings carefully.
If anyone tried escaping from below, he would intercept them.
He also occasionally glanced at the notifications connected to his summons.
If one of the skeletons died, he would know instantly.
Luckily, nothing unusual happened.
Around fifteen minutes later, Celeste jumped back onto the edge of the canyon.
She looked extremely satisfied.
"I killed thirty of them," she said while laughing slightly. "They were all hiding like rats."
Leon raised his eyebrows, "...Damn."
It wasn’t exactly Leon’s style to hunt people who were hiding and avoiding combat.
But the event forced everyone into this situation.
Survival meant eliminating others. So he simply accepted it.
Time continued to pass.
The hours slowly slipped by as Leon and Celeste continued hunting.
The number of remaining players kept dropping.
Ding!
[Only 3,000 Players remain.]
Later—
Ding!
[Only 1,500 Players remain.]
And eventually—
Ding!
[Only 500 Players remain.]
At this point, the event had slowed down dramatically. A kill only happened every minute or so.
The remaining players had adapted their strategies.
Some players formed massive alliances of nearly one hundred people.
Their goal was simple: overwhelm anyone they encountered with numbers.
Others chose the opposite approach.
They fought alone or in very small teams because they trusted their own strength.
Leon and Celeste belonged to the second group.
Slash!
Leon cut through the chest of a player who had attempted to ambush him.
At the same moment, Celeste stabbed another player who had been fighting alongside him.
Both enemies disappeared instantly.
Leon glanced toward the participant counter.
Beep!
[Players left: 487.]
He sighed, "It’s going to take forever at this point, I wish we could just eliminate everyone else instantly."
Unfortunately, that wasn’t possible.
The remaining players were either hiding extremely well or traveling in large groups.
All Leon and Celeste could do was continue hunting while waiting for the number to decrease.
At least one thing was certain: their positions in the ranking were now completely secure.
The third player, [DemonBeast], and the fourth player, [MightyElf], were far behind them.
Even if those players somehow eliminated dozens of enemies, they still wouldn’t reach Leon or Celeste.
That meant the best rewards for the event were already within reach.
As long as Leon and Celeste didn’t get eliminated themselves.
"Alright," Leon said.
Fwoosh!
He and Celeste dashed forward again.
This time they were heading back toward the [Citadel of Dusk].
If any players were still hiding, that fortress would be the perfect place.
On the way there, they encountered several more players.
Each of them was quickly eliminated.
Ding!
[You have entered the "Citadel of Dusk"]
The dark fortress stood before them once again.
By now, roughly eleven hours had passed since the event began.
It was very likely that many players had chosen this location as their final hiding place.
"Use your [Flame Sense] again," Leon asked, "But watch out, in this place, they can both hide and ambush."
At the same time, Leon activated one of his own abilities.
Vision Enhancement!
His eyes glowed faintly.
The skill allowed him to see more clearly in the deep darkness surrounding the fortress.
Ding!
[Players Left: 407.]
’Only a few more...’
The two of them stepped into the citadel. Dark corridors stretched in every direction.
Broken walls and ruined towers created endless hiding spots.
But Pyra’s ability made searching much easier.
Whenever the phoenix detected body heat nearby, Leon and Celeste would move toward the location.
One by one, hidden players were discovered.
Some tried to fight. Others tried to run. None of them succeeded.
Nearly an hour passed as they explored the citadel.
Eventually Celeste stretched her arms slightly.
"So... do we keep looking?" she asked with a grin.
Then she added, "We’ve been fighting for almost twelve hours now."
Even Celeste, who loved combat, was starting to feel tired.
Pyra also looked exhausted.
The small phoenix chirped weakly before returning to rest inside Celeste’s chest.
Her body disappeared into the glowing [Pet Space].
Leon nodded, "Yeah, alright."
He looked around the dark fortress one last time.
"We already did what we wanted anyway."
Then he added,
"Let’s go somewhere that isn’t this depressing."
Celeste laughed softly.
The two of them exited the citadel and returned to the nearby forest.
They walked through the dense trees of the [Divine Jungle].
For a few minutes, everything seemed quiet.
Then suddenly—
The forest opened up. They stepped into a clearing neither of them had seen before.
The moment Leon saw what stood there... He stopped walking.
At the center of the clearing stood a massive demonic beast.
Its enormous body towered above the trees. Dark energy pulsed around its skin.
Its glowing eyes slowly turned toward them. Celeste felt a cold chill run down her spine.
The creature’s presence alone was terrifying.
Leon, however, simply raised his sword calmly. A faint smile appeared on his face.
’Oh well.’

chapters.title: Chapter 164: Meeting DemonBeast, End of the Divine Academy’s Event
paragraphs: Leon and Celeste stood still as the massive demonic creature stared directly at them.
Its crimson eyes glowed faintly in the darkness of the clearing.
For a few seconds, no one moved.
The monster looked like a giant wolf, easily three meters tall, with a massive body covered in dark fur.
Crimson cracks ran across its skin like glowing veins, pulsing faintly with demonic energy.
Its mouth slowly opened, revealing several rows of long, razor-sharp teeth.
Two curved horns rose from the sides of its head, just behind its ears.
But what caught Leon’s attention the most were its claws.
They glinted faintly in the dim light, sharp enough to tear through armor like paper.
Leon also noticed something else.
Tiny glowing particles were fading into the air near the edge of the clearing.
Those particles only appeared when players were eliminated.
This creature had killed someone only seconds before Leon and Celeste arrived.
Celeste tightened her grip on her spear.
"What do we do?" she asked quietly. "That thing is strong. I can feel it."
Leon remained calm, "There shouldn’t be monsters inside this event," he said slowly, "Which means that thing isn’t a monster."
He looked directly at the wolf, "It’s a pet."
Without hesitation, Leon activated his ability.
Appraisal!
[Demonic Wolf]
[Level: 9]
[Rank: Mythical]
[Skills: ???]
[Combat Power: ???]
Leon studied the information carefully.
"Hm."
A Mythical-rank beast. That alone made it extremely rare.
Leon’s own pet, the [Primordial Dragon of Chaos], was obviously stronger, and Celeste’s [Queen of Phoenix] talent was also superior.
But that didn’t mean this wolf was weak. Not even close.
In fact, this beast was incredibly dangerous.
Even though it was only level 9, the way pet levels worked was very different from player levels.
A level 9 mythical beast could easily defeat players around level 75 or even higher.
And while Pyra was a higher-ranked creature overall, she was still young and underleveled.
Right now, the demonic wolf was definitely stronger than her.
Leon slowly shifted his stance slightly. If a fight broke out, he was ready.
He had faced much worse enemies before.
Still, something about the situation felt strange.
And then... a voice suddenly echoed from above the beast.
"Stop, Vex."
Leon and Celeste both looked up at the same time.
And only then did they notice something surprising.
Someone was sitting on the wolf’s back. Leon immediately activated [Appraisal] again.
[ID: DemonBeast]
[Level: 74]
[World: Delsos (High-Level World)]
[Talent: ???]
[Skills: ???]
[Combat Power: ???]
[Details: A member of the demon race who appears to specialize in controlling and fighting with beasts.]
Leon narrowed his eyes slightly. So this was [DemonBeast].
The player currently sitting in third place on the ranking.
The man sitting on the wolf slowly stood up.
He looked extremely imposing.
He was roughly two meters tall, with crimson skin and two large demonic horns curving upward from his head.
His eyes carried the same faint red glow as his pet.
He grinned widely when he looked at Leon.
"You are Celestial," DemonBeast said.
Leon didn’t answer. But DemonBeast didn’t seem to mind.
"I’m not willing to fight you," he continued calmly.
Celeste didn’t relax her stance at all.
"What do we do?" she whispered to Leon. "I think his pet is stronger than Pyra."
Leon didn’t answer immediately.
Instead, he quietly observed the man standing before them.
’DemonBeast...’
Leon searched his memory.
In his previous life, he didn’t recall anyone with that ID causing major problems later on.
Which meant this person probably wasn’t one of the major threats in the future.
’Or maybe he died early,’ Leon thought.
Either way, the man didn’t seem hostile. DemonBeast also looked very confident.
Not arrogant like some other players. Just calm.
Like someone who knew exactly what he was capable of.
Leon finally spoke
"Alright," he said simply, "You can go."
Celeste blinked slightly. But she trusted Leon’s judgment.
Leon himself believed he could win if they fought.
But that didn’t mean fighting was the best choice right now.
DemonBeast nodded once.
"Good." Then he lightly tapped the side of his pet. The demonic wolf turned around.
"I didn’t want to release theothersanyway," DemonBeast added casually.
Leon raised an eyebrow, "The others?"
But before he could ask anything else—
Fwoosh!
The massive wolf sprinted forward at incredible speed.
Within seconds, DemonBeast and his pet disappeared back into the depths of the [Divine Jungle].
Celeste stared in the direction they had gone.
"What the hell was that?" she muttered, "I really thought we were going to fight."
Leon simply shrugged, "Oh well."
He crossed his arms casually.
"He’s in third place, but it’s not like he can catch up to us anymore."
Celeste nodded slowly.
Still... Leon silently memorized that encounter.
Something about that guy felt... interesting. And especially that final comment.
It sounded like DemonBeast had more beasts under his control.
’I’ll keep that in mind,’ Leon thought.
Then Leon looked around the clearing. After a moment, a small grin appeared on his face.
"Alright," he said, "I think we can rest here for a bit."
Fwoosh!
The skeletons he had summoned quickly spread out around the clearing.
They positioned themselves in different directions like guards.
Anyone who tried to enter the clearing would be detected instantly.
Leon leaned back against one of the trees.
"You can rest," he told Celeste. "I’ll keep watch."
Celeste didn’t argue. She was clearly exhausted after fighting for so many hours.
"Thanks," she said softly.
She sat down against another tree nearby and closed her eyes.
Within minutes, she had fallen asleep. Leon remained awake.1
His expression was calm as he stared quietly across the clearing.
The night air moved gently through the trees.
Time slowly passed. Leon used the quiet moment to think.
A lot had happened recently. And even more would happen soon.
’Once this event is over,’ he thought, ’I’ll finally gain access to the [Divine Academy].’
That was the entire point of participating in the event.
But Leon had no interest in becoming a normal student.
None of that mattered to him. The academy itself was what interested him.
More specifically...The people running it.
’The teachers... and the chairman.’
Leon would never forget them.
Just like he had destroyed the [Church of Light] and the [Shadow Assassin Guild], he intended to remove as many dangerous organizations as possible from the [Higher Domains].
And the [Divine Academy] was one of them.
The teachers and the chairman were all extremely powerful.
Most of them were around level 100. Taking them down wouldn’t be easy.
In fact, it might take weeks of preparation. But Leon wasn’t in a hurry.
As long as he acted before they gained even more power, he would have a chance.
The most important step right now was simply getting inside the academy.
And this event would give him that opportunity.
Hours continued to pass. The participant counter slowly kept dropping.
Ding!
[Players left: 300.]
Later—
Ding!
[Players left: 200.]
Leon barely reacted.
He simply continued watching the clearing while his skeletons patrolled the area.
And eventually, when the number of players dropped to around 150, Celeste finally woke up.
She stretched slightly before standing up.
"You should rest now while—"
"It’s fine," Leon interrupted with a grin, "I don’t get tired easily."
Celeste tilted her head slightly.
After using [Oblivion Meteor] twice and getting stronger, Leon knew his endurance was extremely high.
Compared to normal players, his stamina was almost endless.
Celeste laughed slightly, "Alright then."
The two of them left the clearing. They began searching for the last remaining players.
At this stage, everyone left was strong. Some were hiding extremely well.
Others were hunting just like Leon and Celeste. But it didn’t matter.
It only took about an hour before the final panel appeared.
Ding!
[Only 100 players remain in the event.]
Leon stopped walking. Another message immediately followed.
Ding!
[The "Divine Academy Examination" is now over.]
[The top 10 participants will receive their rewards shortly.]
Leon couldn’t help but grin. He opened the ranking window one more time.
And the very top...
[1. Celestial: 2,547 Points.]
And right below him—
[2. UndyingPhoenix: 1,794 Points.]
He and Celeste had completely dominated the event. And it wasn’t even close.

sentences.text: Leon and Celeste stood still as the massive demonic creature stared directly at them.
Its crimson eyes glowed faintly in the darkness of the clearing.
For a few seconds, no one moved.
The monster looked like a giant wolf, easily three meters tall, with a massive body covered in dark fur.
Crimson cracks ran across its skin like glowing veins, pulsing faintly with demonic energy.
Its mouth slowly opened, revealing several rows of long, razor-sharp teeth.
Two curved horns rose from the sides of its head, just behind its ears.
But what caught Leon’s attention the most were its claws.
They glinted faintly in the dim light, sharp enough to tear through armor like paper.
Leon also noticed something else.
Tiny glowing particles were fading into the air near the edge of the clearing.
Those particles only appeared when players were eliminated.
This creature had killed someone only seconds before Leon and Celeste arrived.
Celeste tightened her grip on her spear.
"What do we do?" she asked quietly.
"That thing is strong.
I can feel it."
Leon remained calm, "There shouldn’t be monsters inside this event," he said slowly, "Which means that thing isn’t a monster."
He looked directly at the wolf, "It’s a pet."
Without hesitation, Leon activated his ability.
Appraisal!
[Demonic Wolf]
[Level: 9]
[Rank: Mythical]
[Skills: ???]
[Combat Power: ???]
Leon studied the information carefully.
"Hm."
A Mythical-rank beast.
That alone made it extremely rare.
Leon’s own pet, the [Primordial Dragon of Chaos], was obviously stronger, and Celeste’s [Queen of Phoenix] talent was also superior.
But that didn’t mean this wolf was weak.
Not even close.
In fact, this beast was incredibly dangerous.
Even though it was only level 9, the way pet levels worked was very different from player levels.
A level 9 mythical beast could easily defeat players around level 75 or even higher.
And while Pyra was a higher-ranked creature overall, she was still young and underleveled.
Right now, the demonic wolf was definitely stronger than her.
Leon slowly shifted his stance slightly.
If a fight broke out, he was ready.
He had faced much worse enemies before.
Still, something about the situation felt strange.
And then... a voice suddenly echoed from above the beast.
"Stop, Vex."
Leon and Celeste both looked up at the same time.
And only then did they notice something surprising.
Someone was sitting on the wolf’s back.
Leon immediately activated [Appraisal] again.
[ID: DemonBeast]
[Level: 74]
[World: Delsos (High-Level World)]
[Talent: ???]
[Skills: ???]
[Combat Power: ???]
[Details: A member of the demon race who appears to specialize in controlling and fighting with beasts.]
Leon narrowed his eyes slightly.
So this was [DemonBeast].
The player currently sitting in third place on the ranking.
The man sitting on the wolf slowly stood up.
He looked extremely imposing.
He was roughly two meters tall, with crimson skin and two large demonic horns curving upward from his head.
His eyes carried the same faint red glow as his pet.
He grinned widely when he looked at Leon.
"You are Celestial," DemonBeast said.
Leon didn’t answer.
But DemonBeast didn’t seem to mind.
"I’m not willing to fight you," he continued calmly.
Celeste didn’t relax her stance at all.
"What do we do?" she whispered to Leon.
"I think his pet is stronger than Pyra."
Leon didn’t answer immediately.
Instead, he quietly observed the man standing before them.
’DemonBeast...’
Leon searched his memory.
In his previous life, he didn’t recall anyone with that ID causing major problems later on.
Which meant this person probably wasn’t one of the major threats in the future.
’Or maybe he died early,’ Leon thought.
Either way, the man didn’t seem hostile.
DemonBeast also looked very confident.
Not arrogant like some other players.
Just calm.
Like someone who knew exactly what he was capable of.
Leon finally spoke
"Alright," he said simply, "You can go."
Celeste blinked slightly.
But she trusted Leon’s judgment.
Leon himself believed he could win if they fought.
But that didn’t mean fighting was the best choice right now.
DemonBeast nodded once.
"Good." Then he lightly tapped the side of his pet.
The demonic wolf turned around.
"I didn’t want to release theothersanyway," DemonBeast added casually.
Leon raised an eyebrow, "The others?"
But before he could ask anything else—
Fwoosh!
The massive wolf sprinted forward at incredible speed.
Within seconds, DemonBeast and his pet disappeared back into the depths of the [Divine Jungle].
Celeste stared in the direction they had gone.
"What the hell was that?" she muttered, "I really thought we were going to fight."
Leon simply shrugged, "Oh well."
He crossed his arms casually.
"He’s in third place, but it’s not like he can catch up to us anymore."
Celeste nodded slowly.
Still...
Leon silently memorized that encounter.
Something about that guy felt... interesting.
And especially that final comment.
It sounded like DemonBeast had more beasts under his control.
’I’ll keep that in mind,’ Leon thought.

After a moment, a small grin appeared on his face.
"Alright," he said, "I think we can rest here for a bit."

The skeletons he had summoned quickly spread out around the clearing.
They positioned themselves in different directions like guards.
Anyone who tried to enter the clearing would be detected instantly.
Leon leaned back against one of the trees.

"I’ll keep watch."

She was clearly exhausted after fighting for so many hours.

None of that mattered to him.
The academy itself was what interested him.
More specifically...The people running it.
’The teachers... and the chairman.’
Leon would never forget them.

And the [Divine Academy] was one of them.
The teachers and the chairman were all extremely powerful.
Most of them were around level 100.
Taking them down wouldn’t be easy.

chapters.title: Chapter 165: Entering the Divine Academy, To the Event Hall
paragraphs: Fwoosh! Ding!
[You have completed the "Divine Academy Examination" and have been accepted into "Divine Academy"]
[You are free to come or not, our main purpose is to help you enhance your powers and become useful =)]
Leon stared at the second line with a blank expression, his eyes lingering on the words for a few seconds.
Even someone who didn’t know anything about the gods could see that these guys had ulterior motives.

"This academy is weird," Celeste said while crossing her arms, her brows slightly furrowed as she looked at where the message had been. "But everyone keeps saying it’s amazing and that it helps them increase their abilities really fast..."
Leon glanced at her with a faint grin, "Do you want to go?"
Celeste thought about it for barely a second before shaking her head.
"Nah," she replied casually. "I have a bad feeling about it, and I prefer to stay with you~"
"Alright."
It seemed Celeste’s intuition wasn’t bad at all.
She could immediately tell that something about the academy felt suspicious.
Still, the two of them didn’t have much time to think about it.
Ding!
[You shall receive your rewards soon.]
The moment that final panel appeared before the hundred remaining players...
Fwoosh!
Their bodies instantly began dissolving into glowing particles.
The clearing, the trees, the battlefield of the examination, everything slowly disappeared as the teleportation effect swallowed them.
And after a few seconds...
Ding!
[You have arrived at "Divine Academy City"]
[Please enter the "Divine Academy" and listen to the chairman’s speech to claim your first place reward!]
Leon raised an eyebrow slightly as he read the new notification.
Celeste received a similar panel, except hers stated that she would receive the second place reward.
"Do we really need to?" she groaned, clearly not excited about the idea.
"Yeah," Leon replied calmly.
He didn’t like it either, but missing out on a reward from an event like this would be a waste.
Considering how large and influential the academy was, the reward for first place was almost guaranteed to be something valuable.
"Let’s just get this over with."
Fortunately, Leon and Celeste had one major advantage.
Even if something went wrong inside the academy... dying wasn’t actually that dangerous for them.
Celeste would revive after three days thanks to her phoenix-race nature.
And Leon had even more safety measures.
His [Life Vessel] title alone would resurrect him instantly on the spot if he died.
On top of that, he still possessed a [Resurrection Stone].
In other words, even if the academy tried something strange, they weren’t exactly risking everything.
"We’ll leave the moment we get our rewards," Leon said as they began walking forward. "Then I want to check what’s inside the gate in the [Vine Plains].
"Same," Celeste nodded. "I was thinking about it the entire event."
The mysterious gate had been on both of their minds for quite a while now.
But at that moment, Leon suddenly glanced at something else.
More precisely... his [World Map].
And even more specifically... The [Domain Travel] cooldown.
Beep!
[Domain Travel Cooldown: 7 Hours 51 Minutes 46 Seconds.]
"Hm."
Leon thought about it for a moment.
Since the Divine Academy event had lasted around twelve hours, that meant the cooldown had already been reduced quite a lot.
If his guess was correct, by the time they finished investigating the [Ancient Gate] in the [Vine Plains], the cooldown would probably be over.
Which meant he would finally be able to travel again, to [Higher Domain #3].
That was where Emilia currently was.
He hadn’t seen her since they entered the [Higher Domains], and he was curious about what she was doing.
He was also eager to see what was in [Higher Domain #3] as the areas there would be much more different.
And once he was done, he still planned to get back to [Higher Domain #1].
’I also want to go back to [Higher Domain #54],’ Leon thought, ’It’s the one I know best among them all.’
Unfortunately, the biggest limitation right now was the one-day cooldown on [Domain Travel].
’I wonder if there’s a way to reduce it,’ Leon thought quietly.
Maybe there were items or titles capable of shortening the cooldown.
Or perhaps some hidden mechanic within the system.
Traveling between domains using the "normal" method was also possible, but that process was more complicated.
For now though, Leon pushed those thoughts aside and looked around.
He, Celeste, and the rest of the top one hundred players had appeared in the massive square directly in front of the academy.
The players who had been eliminated earlier in the event had been teleported somewhere outside the city.
The square was still lively, but noticeably less crowded than before.
Several players were already discussing the event, some celebrating their placements while others complained about their losses.
Leon ignored all of them.
His eyes focused on the massive structure standing ahead: the [Divine Academy].
The building itself was enormous, towering high above the surrounding structures with white stone walls and golden decorations covering the exterior.
Large pillars lined the entrance, giving the entire place an imposing and almost sacred atmosphere.
Without hesitation, Leon began walking toward it.
Celeste followed right beside him. They soon reached the entrance.
But unlike the first time he had tried to enter...
Ding!
[You are allowed to enter the "Divine Academy"]
"Hm."
The barrier that had blocked Leon previously was gone.
He stepped forward without hesitation.
"See, wasn’t so hard, was it?"
A familiar voice suddenly sounded beside him.
Leon slowly turned his head.
Standing there with a wide smile was the same teacher he had encountered earlier: Alikar.
The man who had previously threatened him.
This time though, Alikar’s attitude had completely changed.
"I didn’t expect you to be this strong, Celestial," he said with a grin. "You are welcome here anytime."
"Sure..." Leon replied flatly.
He didn’t bother continuing the conversation.
Instead, he simply turned around and walked forward, completely ignoring the man.
Celeste leaned slightly closer to Leon as they stepped inside the academy.
"What’s his problem?" she whispered.
"Don’t know," Leon replied calmly. "But he isn’t a good guy."
He paused briefly before adding, "None of them are."
As soon as they passed through the entrance, they stepped into a massive hall.
The interior of the academy was just as grand as its exterior.
High ceilings stretched far above them, decorated with glowing crystals that illuminated the entire hall.
Students walked around in groups, talking among themselves.
They came from all kinds of races.
Some of them even had appearances Leon couldn’t immediately identify.
Still, Leon didn’t care about any of that. He simply looked forward.
But before he could even think about where to go next...
Ding!
[Head to the "Event Hall" to receive your reward.]
A golden arrow suddenly appeared in front of them.
It floated in the air, pointing toward one of the corridors deeper inside the academy.
They both glanced at each other for a moment, neither of them said anything.
Then they both shrugged, "Let’s go."
They followed the arrow.
The halls of the academy were enormous, filled with various rooms, training areas, and gathering spaces.
Even after several minutes of walking, they still hadn’t reached their destination.
Eventually though... They stopped in front of a massive door.
Ding!
[This is the "Event Hall"]
[Listen to the chairman’s speech and he shall reward you all with your respective rewards.]
Leon stared at the door silently.
From the other side... He could feel a powerful aura.
Celeste clearly felt it too. But neither of them stepped back.
They REALLY wanted those rewards
And if listening to some speech was the price they had to pay... Then so be it.
Creak!
Leon pushed the massive door open. And he stepped inside the [Event Hall].

chapters.title: Chapter 166: The Divine Academy’s Chairman, Dominik’s Speech
paragraphs: Fwoosh!
The moment Leon stepped into the [Event Hall], his eyes slowly swept across the entire room while he calmly analyzed everything around him.
The hall itself was enormous, with towering pillars rising toward the high ceiling and golden light illuminating the polished stone floor beneath their feet.
The atmosphere inside felt noticeably heavier than the rest of the academy.
Eight figures were already standing inside.
His gaze moved across them one by one, quickly recognizing several familiar faces among the group: [MightyElf] and [DemonBeast].
Both of them had been near the top of the rankings during the event, which meant the rest of the individuals present were most likely the remaining players who had secured spots within the top ten.
"We meet again, Celestial," DemonBeast laughed loudly while crossing his arms.
Leon didn’t respond immediately, his expression remaining calm as he studied the man standing a few meters away.
"I knew he would be the one in first place the moment I saw him," another player, LasagnaCat, spoke while adjusting the crimson robe resting on his shoulders, "It was quite obvious from the start."

"He had a [Global Announcement] after all," RulerOfVines added with a nod, he was surrounded by several twisting vines that slowly moved around his body, "Makes sense that he would dominate the event."
A few others murmured in agreement while glancing toward Leon and Celeste.
As for Azaroth, known as [MightyElf], he didn’t say anything at all.
His sharp eyes briefly met Leon’s for a fraction of a second before looking away again.
The two of them had already encountered each other once before inside the [Poison Forest] located in [Lower Domain #1], but Azaroth didn’t make any effort to reveal that fact to the others.
Leon noticed the brief glance, though he didn’t react to it.
He didn’t particularly care whether the man acknowledged him or not.
At that moment, however, Leon could clearly feel something else.
Every single person in the hall was looking at him.
Their gazes contained curiosity, caution, and in some cases even a bit of competitive tension.
After all, he had just taken first place in an event involving tens of thousands of players.
Naturally, people would be interested.

"As for the girl beside him..." DemonBeast continued while his grin widened slightly, his sharp eyes shifting toward Celeste. "I think she’s strong too. I could feel an extremely powerful beast inside of her earlier."
Celeste simply nodded slightly in response.
In truth, she didn’t trust a single person standing in that hall.
Eye of Fury!1
Without anyone noticing, Celeste quietly activated her ability and began examining the status panels of the surrounding players.
Her golden eyes briefly glowed with faint energy as the information appeared before her vision.
After a few seconds, she leaned slightly toward Leon.
"All of them are level 72 to 75," she whispered quietly. "And their [Combat Power] values are pretty high."
Leon nodded slowly when he heard that information.
Still, his expression didn’t change.
Even though the players present were strong, none of them made him feel particularly threatened.
Without saying anything else, Leon calmly walked forward toward the center of the room.
The others watched him move, but before anyone could start another conversation...
Fwoosh!
A violent explosion of energy suddenly erupted above them.
Everyone immediately reacted.
Several players instinctively stepped back while activating their skills or raising defensive stances.
Even DemonBeast’s expression hardened as he looked upward.
A thick cloud of mist spread across the ceiling of the hall.
And from within that mist... A figure slowly descended.
Leon’s eyes narrowed slightly.
Appraisal!
[Divine Academy Chairman, Dominik]
[Level: 100]
[Talent: ???]
[Combat Power: ???]
[Details: The chairman of Divine Academy, very powerful and seems to be empowered by something.]
The moment the man fully appeared...
BOOM!
An overwhelming aura exploded throughout the entire hall.
The pressure crashed down on everyone like a massive wave, causing the air itself to feel heavier.
Several players instantly dropped to one knee.
Others trembled while struggling to stay standing.
"What the hell is this power...?"
"He’s level 100 so it makes sense but... holy hell..."
"This pressure is insane..."
Even Celeste’s legs momentarily buckled beneath the weight of the aura.
Still, she gritted her teeth and forced herself to remain standing.
As for Leon... He didn’t move at all.
Unshaken!
The passive effect of his title activated instantly, completely nullifying the fear effect radiating from Dominik’s aura.
Not even a trace of intimidation reached him.
The chairman noticed that immediately. A wide smile slowly spread across his face.
"Heh."
Dominik let out a short laugh as he waved his hand casually, causing the overwhelming aura filling the hall to disappear instantly.
The players finally breathed again as the pressure vanished.
"Interesting."
Dominik then dropped down to the ground with a quiet thud, allowing everyone to clearly see him for the first time.
He was a tall man, standing close to two meters in height, with neatly combed white hair and a short beard framing his sharp jawline.
His appearance gave off an air of refined elegance.
The uniform he wore was clearly the academy’s official attire, marked with an elaborate insignia across the chest.

"We usually host a celebration for those who successfully enter the academy," Dominik began speaking while calmly clasping his hands behind his back. "But the top ten participants are a special case, so we prefer to meet them separately."
The players slowly relaxed after hearing his words.
Some still looked cautious. Others already seemed impressed by his presence.
Only Leon and Celeste remained completely unreadable.

He slowly paced across the hall while speaking.
"And perhaps, if some of you stay here long enough... you might even become as strong as I am."
Those words clearly caught the attention of several players.
The idea of reaching level 100 alone was enough to excite almost anyone.
After all, someone that powerful would enjoy wealth, status, and influence across the [Higher Domains].
"In fact..." Dominik suddenly snapped his fingers.
Snap!
A sword instantly appeared in his right hand.
And at the same time, a glowing sphere of flames formed above his left palm.

"I happen to be quite proficient in both swordsmanship and magic," he said proudly. "Which means that the top ten participants of this event will receive something special in addition to their rewards."
He paused briefly.
"You will have the opportunity to train under my guidance."

The idea of receiving personal training from someone as powerful as Dominik seemed almost unbelievable.

His smile widened slightly.

"Come one by one, starting from the lowest rank and finishing with the first place."

"Damn, this is really good..."

Fwoosh!
A bright flash of light filled the hall.
A small ornate box materialized in the air before Dominik, slowly floating in place.

He grabbed the box and immediately stored it inside his [Storage Space].

Fwoosh!
He vanished in a cloud of smoke.

Ding!
[Ascendant Skill Scroll: Will grant the user an ascendant-rank skill that fits them.]

He stared at it carefully.
Appraisal!
[Divine Box (???): Holds 5 powerful items. Upon opening it, the user will receive one of them.]
Leon stared at the box for several seconds. Then a slow smile spread across his face.

chapters.title: Chapter 167: The Divine Box’s Rewards
paragraphs: While examining the [Divine Box], Celeste found herself even more impressed than she had been when she first looked at her own reward.
The box itself looked rather simple at first glance, yet the aura coming from it was unmistakably powerful.
Still though, Celeste had already assumed something obvious.
"Too bad you can only get one of the five items—"
But she suddenly stopped mid-sentence.
Her eyes widened slightly as the thought fully formed in her mind.
"—Wait a damn minute."
Leon had already reached the exact same conclusion, and the two of them exchanged a glance that said everything without needing any further explanation.
Leon’s talent was [100% Drop Rate].
Normally, the [Divine Box] clearly stated that opening it would grant the user only one of the five items inside.
But talents that affected drop rates were strange.
The system didn’t always follow normal logic when those kinds of abilities were involved.
So the real question became simple.
Would the talent treat the contents of the box like a drop table?
Or would it follow the restriction written in the description?
There was only one way to find out.
Leon lifted the box slightly and began pouring his mana directly into it.
The moment his energy flowed into the artifact, the [Divine Box] reacted instantly.
A powerful glow erupted from its surface as ancient symbols carved into the lid began shining with bright golden light.
Everyone still standing inside the [Event Hall] quickly turned their heads toward Leon as the box slowly floated into the air.
It began rotating slowly while the energy around it intensified.
Fwoosh!
The light grew brighter and brighter until the entire hall was illuminated.
And then—
Ding!
[You have opened the "Divine Box".]
For a split second, nothing happened.
But immediately afterward—
Ding!
[100% Drop Rate has triggered, all items inside of the Divine Box will be placed into your storage space.]
Leon felt a surge of excitement inside his chest.
"I knew it," he laughed internally, trying his best to keep his expression calm despite the massive success.
He had honestly hesitated for a moment before opening the box because the description clearly stated that only one item would be granted.
But as long as luck or drop mechanics were involved, Leon’s talent would always override the restriction.
Every single reward inside the box had just been given to him.
"All five of them..." Leon thought with a grin.
Normally, the person in first place would only receive one random reward.
But thanks to [100% Drop Rate], Leon had just obtained everything.
He didn’t waste a single second before opening his [Storage Space] to check what had appeared inside.
And when the items appeared before his eyes, even Leon couldn’t help but smile.
There were five treasures resting neatly inside his storage.
A [Resurrection Stone], an [Ascendant Skill Scroll], a [Divine Key], a [Secret Realm Token].
And finally... A piece of equipment labeled [Divine Armor].
"Lots of amazing items," Leon murmured with clear satisfaction while examining the rewards.
He immediately began analyzing each one carefully.The first item was the most familiar.
[Resurrection Stone (Legendary): Will revive someone at the nearest "safe point" upon death. Automatically consumed if the user dies.]
This one was very straightforward.
And Leon was genuinely happy to receive another one.
The resurrection item he currently had was extremely valuable, but having an additional one provided a huge safety net.
If his [Life Vessel] title was ever consumed and he died again afterward, the [Resurrection Stone] would activate and bring him back at the nearest safe location.
In other words, it was an extra life.
For someone constantly fighting powerful enemies, that kind of item was priceless.
Next, Leon examined the second reward: the [Ascendant Skill Scroll].
It was exactly the same type of scroll Celeste had just received moments ago.
Celeste stared at Leon with disbelief when she realized this.
"Hold on," she said slowly while crossing her arms. "So you basically got my reward... and four other items on top of it?"
Leon shrugged casually, "Looks like it."
Celeste shook her head with a sigh, "Holy hell."
For a normal player, receiving just one of these rewards would already be incredible.
But Leon had casually obtained all of them thanks to his talent.
It was honestly unfair. Still, Leon moved on to the next item.
[Secret Realm Token (Mythical): Can be used in a place where a secret realm resides to open it. Do note that it is extremely dangerous.]
It was yet another item that he already knew about, though Leon knew it would be extremely useful.
’You never know when you’ll discover a [Secret Realm],’ he grinned, ’Very good.’
Having a [Secret Realm Token] meant he could instantly open one of those realms if he found the correct location.
Now only two items remained. The first one was the equipment.
Fwoosh!
Leon inspected it carefully as its panel appeared.
[Divine Armor (Ascendant): +10,000 Defense, +5,000 Spirit, +5,000 Strength, +4,000 Agility, +3,000 Constitution. Requirement: Be in the top 10 of the "Divine Academy Event"]
"Wow."
Leon genuinely paused when he saw those numbers.
This armor was easily the best defensive equipment he had encountered since arriving in this new life.
It was even stronger than the [Elemental Dragon Armor +2] he was currently wearing.
Without hesitation, Leon removed his old armor and equipped the new one.
The divine armor immediately formed around his body, fitting perfectly as if it had been crafted specifically for him.
The previous armor was stored inside his [Storage Space].
Of course, removing the [Elemental Dragon Armor +2] meant losing the [Storm of Elements] skill from his [Blood Heart]’s blessing.
But Leon didn’t seem worried.
"I’m pretty sure the [Blood Heart] will recharge soon," he thought calmly.
Once it did, he would simply apply another blessing to his new armor, which meant the loss was only temporary.
At that moment, Leon suddenly looked toward Celeste.
"We’ll need to get you two elemental sub-talents," he said thoughtfully.
Celeste tilted her head slightly, "Why?"
Leon opened his storage again and explained the armor’s requirement.
The requirement to equip the [Elemental Dragon Armor +2] was possessing two of the four basic elemental sub-talents.
"I already obtained the [Deep Earth Affinity (B-Level)] from the [Wild Plant King]," he explained while pulling out the scroll representing the sub-talent. "So we only need one more afterward."
Since Leon no longer needed it, Celeste could easily use the armor instead.
He tossed the earth affinity toward her.
Celeste immediately absorbed the sub-talent.
A faint glow surrounded her body for a moment before disappearing.
"Thank you~" she said with a bright smile.
Leon nodded before finally examining the last item. The one he understood the least.
[Divine Key (???): A strange key that emits a divine glow. Perhaps it can be used somewhere.]
Leon stared at the description for several seconds.
The system didn’t provide any hint about where it should be used.
But items with vague descriptions like this were often extremely valuable once their purpose was discovered.
Leon simply stored it again.
"I’m sure it’ll become useful eventually," he thought calmly.
With that, he had finished examining all five rewards.
Leon stretched slightly before turning toward Celeste with a satisfied grin.
"Alright," he said. "We should leave and then use our [Ascendant Skill Scrolls] to learn new skills."
Celeste nodded enthusiastically.
She was extremely curious to see what kind of ability the scroll would grant her.
The two of them began walking toward the exit of the [Event Hall].
Several players noticed them leaving.
Some of them watched carefully, their expressions cautious.
But none of them tried to stop them.
Once Leon and Celeste stepped outside the hall, Leon immediately opened his [World Map].
His finger moved toward a familiar location: [Vine Plains].
"Hold on to me again," Leon said with a grin.
Celeste already knew what he meant. So she grabbed his arm.
"Ready."
Fwoosh!
Their bodies instantly dissolved into particles as the teleportation activated.
Moments later, they reappeared at the entrance of the [Vine Plains].
The area around them was filled with thick vegetation and massive vines twisting through the landscape.
Celeste immediately pulled the [Ascendant Skill Scroll] out of her [Storage Space].
"Alright," she said excitedly. "Let’s see what I get..."
Leon did the exact same. He held the glowing scroll in his hands before slowly pouring his mana into it.
Both of them waited in anticipation, eager to discover what kind of abilities they would receive.

chapters.title: Chapter 168: Phoenix Wings and Crimson Dance, The Ancient Gate is Activated
paragraphs: Fwoosh!
Leon and Celeste stood side by side in the [Vine Plains], both of them holding their respective [Ascendant Skill Scroll] while slowly pouring their mana into them.
The moment enough mana flowed into them, the scrolls suddenly dissolved into thousands of glowing particles that rushed directly into their bodies.
The golden light wrapped around them for a brief moment before disappearing entirely.
Celeste was the first one to receive a notification.
Ding!
[You have learned the skill "Phoenix Wings (Ascendant)"]
"Oh!"
Her eyes instantly lit up with excitement as she opened the panel to inspect the ability she had just acquired, her curiosity practically exploding as she quickly read through the description.
[Phoenix Wings (Ascendant): Can release your phoenix wings to fly into the air for up to one minute. 5-minutes cooldown.]
A huge smile spread across her face as she read the words.
Leon also glanced over the panel from beside her, calmly analyzing the skill for a moment before nodding in approval since the ability was indeed quite impressive.
"I’m mostly surprised you didn’t have wings to begin with," Leon said with a faint grin while crossing his arms.
Celeste immediately turned toward him with a playful expression.
"Phoenix-race people don’t actually have wings, silly," she explained while lightly poking his arm. "We only inherit the immortality trait, but I guess now I have wings too."
Leon nodded slightly since that explanation made sense.
Celeste’s race was already extremely powerful thanks to its natural ability to revive after death.
Being able to fly, even if only for one minute at a time, could change the entire outcome of a battle depending on how it was used.
Still though, Leon’s attention quickly shifted back toward his own system panel.
Because his skill notification had just appeared as well.
Ding!
[You have learned the skill "Crimson Dance (Ascendant)"]
"Oh?"
Leon raised an eyebrow slightly before opening the panel to read the description.
[Crimson Dance (Ascendant): As long as you close the distance with your enemy, you may launch a barrage of crimson slashes at them, each one extremely sharp.]
Leon stared at the description for a few seconds while trying to understand how the ability actually functioned.
Unlike some other skills that clearly explained their mechanics, this one seemed a little vague.
It mentioned launching a barrage of crimson slashes once the distance between him and his opponent was closed.
But it didn’t specify whether those slashes were physical strikes, energy projections, or something else entirely.
Still, despite the unclear explanation, Leon understood one thing very clearly: this was now the strongest skill he possessed.
And the main reason for that was its rank.
[Crimson Dance] was an ascendant-rank ability.
Leon’s previously highest-ranked skill, [Celestial Hand], was only ancient-rank.
Ancient-rank abilities were already incredibly powerful, but ascendant-rank abilities were on an entirely different level.
"I guess I’ll have to test it out later," Leon thought calmly, though a small grin appeared on his face as he imagined the potential destructive power hidden behind the skill.
Celeste meanwhile stretched slightly before speaking again.
"I guess this event wasn’t so bad after all," she said happily while spinning the scroll particles that were still fading around her fingers. "I’ll also be able to fly alongside Pyra now."
Leon nodded, "But we still need to gather a lot of enhancement stones if we want these skills to become truly powerful."
Celeste blinked, "Right...
For ascendant-rank skills, even increasing them to level two required an enormous number of enhancement stones.
Thirty stones just for the first upgrade.
That was an extremely high price compared to other abilities.
Still, powerful skills naturally came with high requirements.
Regardless, Leon soon closed his panels and looked forward again.
"I guess we can proceed now," he said with a grin.
Even though the [Divine Academy Examination] had ended, Leon was fully aware that his involvement with the academy was far from over.
Still, until he became strong enough to challenge the powerful individuals controlling that place, he had no intention of returning.
Leon opened his [World Map] again.
And as he zoomed into the area ahead of them...
"Oh." He suddenly noticed something, "I think we can teleport even closer."
Celeste leaned slightly toward him, "What do you mean?"
Leon looked at the map.
The small dots representing both himself and Celeste were visible on the terrain of the [Vine Plains].
But as he scrolled further ahead across the region, another symbol appeared on the screen.
It was the icon of an ancient gate.
The symbol had a crimson outline surrounding it, and above it were the words: Dangerous.
Leon nodded slowly.
"Makes sense the [World Map] shows it," he murmured. "It did that before."
However, this was the first time he had seen the map label something specifically as dangerous.
And judging by the ominous design of the symbol, whatever was waiting behind that gate was definitely not something ordinary.
"Hold on to me one last time," Leon said with a grin while preparing the teleportation. "We’re heading straight to the gate."
Celeste immediately grabbed his arm.
"Nice," she said happily. "I really didn’t feel like walking through the [Vine Plains] again."
They were both strong enough to easily deal with the monsters roaming the area, but since their objective was the gate itself, teleporting directly there would save a lot of time.
Fwoosh! Ding!
[Do you wish to teleport to "Will of Nature’s Attack Zone"?]
"Yes."
Leon confirmed without hesitation.
The world around them instantly dissolved into swirling particles of light as the teleportation activated.
Moments later, they reappeared at the exact location.
They were now standing right in front of the same transparent veil they had encountered earlier.
Beyond it stretched the massive zone filled with endless vines, and at the very center of that chaotic landscape stood the ancient gate.
Leon didn’t hesitate even for a moment.
He stepped forward and passed directly through the veil.
Celeste followed immediately behind him.
Ding!
[You have entered the "Will of Nature’s Attack Zone."]
Fortunately, both of them still had the [Plant King Flower] resting on top of their heads.
That small item was the only reason the vines weren’t attacking them.
Even Leon could clearly feel the terrifying power contained within the countless vines surrounding the area.
Their energy was dense and aggressive.
’If I didn’t have the [Plant King Flower], would I even reach the gate?’ Leon wondered silently.
For a brief moment, he almost felt tempted to test it.
But the memory of the goblin player who had been thrown into this place earlier quickly convinced him otherwise.
That experiment had already proven how dangerous the zone truly was.
After walking carefully for about a minute, they finally reached the center of the attack zone.
The ancient gate stood before them. It looked exactly the same as before.
Leon also noticed that the symbol displayed on the [World Map] was identical to the real structure standing in front of them.
"So what do we do now?" Celeste asked while observing the hundreds of vines slowly twisting around the gate.
They weren’t attacking. But they were definitely more active near the structure.
Leon stepped forward and placed his hand on the surface of the gate.
And the moment he did—
BOOM!
A violent surge of energy exploded from the ancient structure.
All the vines surrounding the area suddenly began moving.
For a brief moment, Leon thought they were about to attack.
His hand immediately moved toward his sword. But that wasn’t what happened.
Instead, the vines began wrapping around the gate itself.
They tightened around its structure while glowing faintly, transferring their energy directly into the ancient stone until the entire gate started shining with bright green light.
Ding!
[The "Will of Nature’s Gate" has been activated.]
[Step inside if you want to die.]
"...Damn."
The warning was incredibly direct.
Celeste stared at the panel with a slightly uneasy expression.
"...Do we go inside?" she asked slowly while small phoenix flames flickered around her arms. "This seems..."
"Dangerous," Leon finished for her, "But there’s definitely something valuable inside."
He glanced back at the glowing gate, "And I’m not wasting this opportunity."
Celeste sighed before grinning, "Heh... I figured you’d say that."
Without hesitating any further, both of them stepped forward.
And they walked straight through the ancient gate.
Fwoosh!
The world around them twisted violently as the teleportation effect activated again.
A moment later—
Ding!
[You have entered the "Temple of Nature"]
[May the will of the heavenly one be with you, for your death is now certain.]

chapters.title: Chapter 169: The Temple of Nature, Over 500,000 Combat Power
paragraphs: Leon and Celeste appeared in a quiet clearing surrounded by tall trees that stretched far into the sky.
The ground beneath their feet was covered in soft grass, and the air itself felt heavy with natural energy.
Directly in front of them was a massive temple constructed from pale stone and wrapped in enormous vines that crawled across every surface.
’Hm.’
Leon’s eyes narrowed slightly as he studied the temple, though what truly caught his attention wasn’t the structure itself, but the panel that had appeared the moment they arrived.
[May the will of the heavenly one be with you, for your death is now certain.]
This particular version of the phrase somehow sounded even more ominous than any other yet.
Even more so than the "because nothing else will" version.
"Oh well," Leon eventually said with a small shrug as he looked ahead toward the temple’s entrance. "I guess there’s nothing to do but clear this place."
The [Temple of Nature] clearly wasn’t an ordinary zone.
Leon immediately noticed that there had been no prompt asking him to select a difficulty level before entering.
Still, simply reaching this place was already something almost nobody in [Higher Domain #1] could accomplish.
The only entrance to this temple required passing through the terrifying zone protected by the endless vines of the [Will of Nature’s Attack Zone].
Without the protection of the [Plant King Flower], even high-level players would be torn apart instantly before they could get anywhere near the gate.
Perhaps... even level 100 players would die.
In other words, Leon and Celeste had already done something that most players would never even attempt.
Leon slowly stepped forward, his sword resting comfortably in one hand while his staff remained firmly gripped in the other.
But the exact moment he took that step toward the temple—
"Leave."
The single word exploded through the clearing like a thunderclap.
The voice was so powerful that the ground itself seemed to vibrate.
A violent gust of wind erupted outward from the temple’s direction, forcing both Leon and Celeste to shield their faces as their bodies nearly lost balance.
Celeste instinctively raised her arm to protect her eyes, her flames flickering slightly around her as she braced herself against the overwhelming pressure.
’Holy hell, that thing is powerful,’ Leon thought, his eyes widening slightly as he steadied himself.
But despite the terrifying display, Leon knew that they couldn’t leave.
Once they had entered this zone, their only options were to either clear it... or die trying.
Death itself wasn’t particularly frightening to either of them anymore.
Still, that didn’t mean they would treat the challenge lightly.
Leon stepped forward once again.
BOOM!
"You stand... no chance..." the same voice echoed through the temple grounds, its tone filled with absolute confidence. "You are only level 56 and 58... you will never defeat me."
Leon and Celeste instinctively glanced at each other.
If the system expected players around level seventy-five to challenge this place, then technically speaking, they were extremely under-leveled.
But Leon didn’t seem particularly worried.
His eyes briefly shifted downward as he opened his status panel.
"Damn..." Leon muttered quietly.
His total combat power had now surpassed five hundred thousand, resting somewhere around five hundred and twenty thousand after all his equipment and bonuses were calculated.
That number alone was enough to compete with monsters far above his current level.
As for Celeste, she now had around 370,000 Combat Power, which was noticeably lower than Leon’s.
Still, even that amount was already extremely impressive.
"Once we get you the enhancement-type sub-talents," Leon said calmly while glancing at her, "your [Combat Power] will skyrocket."
Celeste nodded slightly as she understood what he meant.
At the moment, she only possessed a single enhancement-type sub-talent: [Strength Enhancement (D-Level)]
It helped, but the rank was far too low to truly unleash her potential.
If Leon managed to obtain something like [Mega Strength Enhancement (A-Level)] or even [Mega Spirit Enhancement (A-Level)] for her, the difference in power would be massive.
With talents like that, Celeste’s combat power could easily rise to match Leon’s.
Leon was actually extremely satisfied with how things were progressing.
Both Celeste and Emilia were capable of keeping up with him despite the insane pace at which his own strength was growing.
Naturally, Leon still possessed far more experience and knowledge due to his previous life, which gave him an advantage in most situations.
But even so, their strength was more than enough to deal with almost anything they encountered.
’They’ll also have to fight the gods and their servants in the future,’ Leon thought quietly as his eyes focused on the temple, ’So this level of power is the bare minimum.’
For a brief moment, Leon hesitated.
There had been many times where he wondered whether it was truly right to drag Celeste and Emilia into a conflict that would eventually involve fighting literal gods.
After all, they would be actually risking their lives fighting those beings.
But...
"Hey, Celeste," Leon suddenly said, breaking the silence.
"Hm?" she responded while tilting her head slightly.
"If you had the strength to do it... would you be willing to fight a god, even if it meant you’d most likely die?"
The question came completely out of nowhere.
Celeste blinked once, clearly surprised by the sudden topic, though it only took her a second before a grin slowly appeared across her face.
"Heh, why not?" she replied casually. "As long as I can fight with you, I guess I’ll take on anything."
Leon simply nodded. That answer was exactly what he expected.
And if Emilia were here instead, he was almost certain she would say something similar.
Which meant that from now on, Leon had only one true priority: to make sure that he, Celeste and Emilia became strong enough to dominate even the gods themselves.
For Emilia, that meant increasing her raw statistics even further, especially since her [Constitution] and [Spirit] were multiplied by five thanks to her unique abilities.
For Celeste, however, things were slightly more complicated.
The first thing Leon wanted to do for her was to obtain another [Ember] to strengthen her talent.
Unfortunately, even Leon had absolutely no idea where such a thing could be found.
"Alright," Leon finally said as he turned his focus back toward the temple. "Let’s just concentrate on clearing the [Temple of Nature]."
This time, as both of them stepped forward once more, the mysterious voice did not echo again.
It had already warned them twice.
At this point, if they still wanted to enter the temple... then so be it.
Leon walked directly toward the massive entrance of the [Temple of Nature], with Celeste following closely behind him.
And the moment they crossed the threshold—
FWOOSH! BAM!
Hundreds of thick vines suddenly erupted from the ground behind them and slammed together with immense force, sealing the entrance completely.
The exit was instantly blocked.
Leon didn’t even bother attempting to cut through them.
Celeste, however, couldn’t help but shudder slightly as she looked at the massive wall of vines now locking them inside.
Then both of them slowly turned their attention forward.
They were standing inside an enormous chamber supported by dozens of ancient stone pillars, all of which were covered in thick vines that had grown across the structure over countless centuries.
In fact, vines were everywhere: the floor, the walls and the ceiling.
The entire temple looked like it had been completely overtaken by nature.
"The [Goddess of Nature] thinks she’s so strong," the same voice from earlier echoed from deep within the chamber. "But once I get out... I’ll show her."
Leon and Celeste immediately focused their gaze toward the far end of the room.
And there... they finally saw it.
A figure was pinned against the wall, completely restrained by hundreds upon hundreds of thick vines that wrapped tightly around its body.
It couldn’t move even a single inch.
The creature itself seemed to be made entirely out of vines as well, its form vaguely humanoid but constantly shifting as the plant-like structure twisted and moved slightly.
Where its eyes should have been, two faint glowing lights flickered with anger.
Leon and Celeste exchanged a brief glance before immediately analyzing the being.
Appraisal!
[Will of Nature (Zone Boss)]
[Level: 75]
[Exclusive Talent: Nature Control (S-Level)]
[Combat Power: 750,000]
[Details: A being that once controlled the nature around "Higher Domain #1", until the "Goddess of Nature" sealed him here forever.]

chapters.title: Chapter 170: The Will of Nature’s Overwhelming Power, Unexpected Death
paragraphs: Leon’s eyes widened slightly at the sight of the [Will of Nature]’s status panel.
Celeste’s reaction was even stronger.
"How... are we supposed to beat that thing?" she muttered quietly while staring at the panel. "That... doesn’t seem doable."
Leon didn’t answer immediately.
Even from this distance, he could feel the terrifying amount of power radiating from the creature.
Still, there was something important.
The [Will of Nature] was still restrained by the divine vines placed by the [Goddess of Nature].
He couldn’t move freely.
"We still need to approach him," Leon eventually said calmly. "But be careful. Even like this, he’s still dangerous."
"Alright."
However, hearing them talk so casually about him seemed to irritate the creature greatly.
"DON’T SPEAK LIKE THIS ABOUT... ME!"
SLASH!
After countless centuries of struggling against the divine restraints, the [Will of Nature] had managed to loosen them slightly.
It wasn’t much. But it was enough.
Suddenly, a vine burst violently from the ground directly behind Celeste and slashed toward her at terrifying speed.
The attack was so fast that Celeste didn’t even have time to react.
Even Leon only noticed the movement at the very last moment.
’Shit,’ Leon thought instantly.
He could probably dodge it himself.
But Celeste, she would definitely be hit.
She would revive eventually, but that process would still take three full days.
So without hesitation...
Fwoosh!
Leon shoved Celeste violently out of the attack’s path while raising his staff to cast his defensive skill.
Darkness Barrier!
A dark shield instantly formed around him. But the vine was far too powerful.
SLASH!
The razor-sharp attack cut straight through the barrier as if it barely existed.
And in the very next instant... Leon’s body was sliced cleanly in half.
There was no time to react to it.
And so as Leon’s consciousness faded, a small system panel quietly appeared before his eyes.
Ding!
[You have died... but it’s not the end yet.]
"LEON!"
Celeste’s voice echoed across the massive chamber as she screamed in disbelief, her eyes widening in pure shock as she watched Leon’s body collapse onto the ground in front of her.
She immediately rushed forward, instinctively spinning her spear in her hands as another vine suddenly burst out of the floor and lashed toward Leon’s fallen body.
Celeste swung her weapon with full force.
CLANG!
The spear deflected the incoming vine just in time, pushing it aside before it could strike Leon again.
But even as she did so, Celeste already knew that it was pointless.
Leon’s body had already been cut cleanly in half.
The upper and lower portions of his body lay separated on the stone floor, completely motionless as blood slowly spread beneath him.
Leon... was actually dead.
"Unlucky for him," the [Will of Nature] said slowly from the far end of the chamber, a wide grin forming across the vine-like structure of his face. "He shouldn’t have underestimated me."
Celeste stood frozen for a moment, staring down at Leon’s lifeless body as her hands trembled slightly around the shaft of her spear.
Her teeth clenched tightly.
’It’s... my fault.’
The thought immediately filled her mind.
If she had noticed the vine sooner... If she had reacted faster...
Leon wouldn’t have needed to push her out of the way.
He wouldn’t have needed to sacrifice himself to protect her.
Still, even with that guilt clawing at her chest, Celeste knew one important thing.
Leon wouldn’t stay dead. He had his [Resurrection Stone].
Eventually, he would come back.
But even knowing that didn’t change the current situation.
Right now... She was alone.
"Alright..." the [Will of Nature] muttered quietly, his glowing eyes flickering with excitement as he focused on the vines restraining his body. "Just a bit more..."
Celeste slowly lifted her head, her expression turning cold, "DIE!"
With a furious shout, she spun her spear and thrust it forward as flames erupted from her hand.
An [Ember Ball] instantly formed in front of her palm before shooting toward the restrained creature at incredible speed.
Fwoosh!
The blazing sphere of fire shot straight across the chamber and slammed directly into the [Will of Nature].
BOOM!
The explosion erupted violently upon impact, flames spreading outward and lighting up the entire temple chamber as scorching heat filled the air.
For a moment, Celeste thought the attack had worked.
But as the flames slowly faded... The [Will of Nature] remained completely unmoved.
Not only that... He was smiling.
"Such powerful flames..." the creature murmured slowly as he observed the vines wrapped around his body.
Celeste’s fire had scorched them badly.
Large sections of the divine vines had blackened and weakened under the intense heat.
"YES... MAGNIFICENT!"
Using every ounce of strength and willpower he possessed, the [Will of Nature] began to struggle violently against his restraints.
His body trembled as the burned vines around his shoulders and arms started to snap one after another.
CRACK! SNAP!
With a violent jerk, the creature finally managed to pull both of his arms free from the divine restraints.
The limbs were monstrous in appearance, made entirely from thick vines, bark-like trunks, and layers of twisting leaves that constantly shifted and moved.
Normally, the divine vines placed by the [Goddess of Nature] would have restrained him forever.
But after so much time passed, Celeste’s flames had weakened them.
And that weakness had given him the opportunity he had been waiting for.
Now that his arms were free... His power immediately increased.
"I appreciate it, phoenix-race girl," the [Will of Nature] said slowly as he extended both of his arms toward Celeste.

Although his chest, legs, and lower body were still tightly bound by countless vines, meaning it would still take years for him to escape completely, simply freeing his arms had already restored a massive portion of his strength.
Only then did Celeste realize the mistake she had made.
Her attack hadn’t damaged him. It had helped him.
Suddenly—
BOOM!
Dozens of vines erupted violently from the stone floor all around her.
Each one was just as sharp and deadly as the vine that had killed Leon moments earlier.
They surrounded her from every direction, twisting through the air like massive spears ready to strike.
"Damn..." Celeste muttered quietly as she tightened her grip on her spear, "I shouldn’t have acted recklessly..."
"DIE!" the [Will of Nature] roared in response.
At that command, every single vine lunged toward her simultaneously.
SLASH! SLASH! SLASH!
The attacks came from every direction. There was no escape.
