chapters.title: Chapter 171: Life Vessel Revival Process, We Aren’t The Same
paragraphs: Meanwhile...
Leon’s vision had gone completely dark the exact moment the vine sliced through his body.
For a brief instant, there had been absolutely nothing.
Not even the feeling of time passing. It was as if the world itself had simply disappeared.
Then, slowly, his awareness returned.
’Damn... I actually died...’
Leon quickly understood what had happened.

The memory of the vine cutting through him replayed clearly in his mind, and he could still remember the terrifying speed of the attack that had pierced through his [Darkness Barrier] as if it didn’t exist.
He had made a mistake.
Even though he reacted quickly and tried to defend himself, the [Will of Nature] was simply far stronger than he had anticipated.
Still... If the same situation happened again...
Leon knew without a single doubt that he would make the exact same decision.
He would push Celeste out of the way. Every single time.
She didn’t have any [Resurrection Stones], which meant that if she died in that temple she would be forced to wait three entire days before respawning.
Leon didn’t want that to happen, especially in a situation where they were facing such a dangerous enemy.
’I’ve got to get back quickly though,’ Leon thought.
As his consciousness stabilized further, Leon slowly looked around.
He was floating in complete darkness.
An endless void stretched in every direction, completely silent and completely empty.
There were no stars, no ground beneath his feet, and no visible walls surrounding him.
It felt as if he was suspended in the middle of nothingness.
’This is...’
Before he could finish that thought—
BOOM!
A powerful explosion suddenly erupted somewhere in front of him, breaking the silence of the void.
A massive structure slowly began to rise from the darkness.
Leon immediately recognized what it was. The [Altar of Life].
The enormous stone altar floated calmly in front of him, glowing with a faint blue light that illuminated the surrounding void.
The structure itself looked ancient, its surface covered with large cracks that spread across the stone like glowing veins.
Despite its damaged appearance, the altar still radiated an immense amount of power.
Ding!
[The power of the "Altar of Life" fuels you, giving you another chance at life.]
Fwoosh...
Suddenly, ten faint figures appeared around the altar.
They were the souls Leon had obtained during the God-Rank Assessment.
Each soul floated silently in the darkness as they slowly surrounded the altar, their ghostly forms faintly glowing as they all turned their attention toward Leon.
For a moment, the void remained completely silent.
"...I still haven’t found the [Lord of Souls]," Leon said quietly while looking at them. "But soon..."
The souls simply stared at him. None of them spoke.
One by one, their bodies began dissolving into glowing particles.
Each soul drifted slowly toward the altar before merging with the stone structure.
The first soul fused with the altar. Then the second. Then the third.
One after another, all ten souls were absorbed.
When the final soul merged with the altar, the entire structure suddenly began shining much brighter than before.
BOOM!
A powerful shockwave erupted outward from the altar.
The wave slammed directly into Leon’s body.
Instantly, an intense burning sensation spread throughout his entire form as enormous amounts of energy surged into him.
Blue cracks appeared across his skin, glowing brightly as the altar’s power flowed through him.
’Holy shit...’
Leon’s eyes widened slightly as the pain intensified.
Just before his consciousness faded again, one final panel appeared in front of him.
Ding!
[The "Altar of Life" has revived you thanks to your "Life Vessel" title.]
[It will take 48 hours for the "Altar of Life" to recharge.]
Leon briefly wondered if there was some way to reduce the recharge time of the [Altar of Life], since waiting two full days for another revival could easily become a problem in the future.
Unfortunately, he didn’t have time to think about it.
His vision faded once again as his consciousness disappeared.
Back in the real world—
At the exact moment the [Will of Nature]’s vines were about to strike Celeste—
Fwoosh!
Blue cracks suddenly began spreading across Leon’s severed body.
A surge of blue energy erupted from within him as the power of the [Altar of Life] activated.
Thin lines of glowing blue energy appeared between the two halves of his body.
They slowly connected the separated parts together.
Then, in less than a second... The two halves fused perfectly.
BOOM!
A powerful explosion burst outward from Leon’s body as he was revived.
The shockwave blasted violently through the chamber, instantly destroying every vine that had been about to strike Celeste.
’I guess the explosion is meant to stop spawn killing...’ Leon thought as he slowly pushed himself to his feet. ’It’s pretty powerful.’
As he stood up, both Celeste and the [Will of Nature] stared at him in shock.
"Leon!" Celeste shouted in relief as she rushed toward him. "B-Be careful! That thing managed to free itself a little because of me!"
Leon turned his gaze toward the creature at the far end of the chamber.
"Did you use fire on it...?" he asked calmly.
"Yes..." Celeste sighed.
Leon could already guess what had happened.
If he had still been alive at the time, he definitely would have told Celeste not to do that.
Using fire against something made entirely out of vines sounded logical at first, but the restraints holding the [Will of Nature] were placed by the [Goddess of Nature] herself.
Burning them would only weaken the seal.
Regardless of the mistake, the situation had already changed.
The [Will of Nature] now had both arms free.
Leon tightened his grip on his sword. Then he nodded calmly.
"Futile," the [Will of Nature] laughed loudly from across the chamber. "That just means I’ll have to kill you again!"
The atmosphere inside the temple immediately grew tense.
For Leon, there was only one clear objective: he needed to get close enough to the [Will of Nature].
Close enough... To strike it directly.
He knew very well that the creature in front of them was far too powerful for ordinary attacks to damage easily.

Even after being restrained for so long by the [Goddess of Nature], the [Will of Nature] still radiated terrifying energy, and it was obvious that his only goal now was to break free completely and destroy everything around him.
Still, Leon had something he wanted to know.
"Do you hate the [Goddess of Nature]?" Leon suddenly asked while taking his stance, his eyes fixed on the creature as he prepared to move at any moment.
For a brief second, the chamber fell silent.
Then, the [Will of Nature] burst into loud laughter.
"HATE?" he shouted as pure fury filled his glowing eyes.
All the vines surrounding him began clenching tightly as his rage surged outward.
"I WILL OBLITERATE HER!" he roared. "AND I WILL MAKE HER REGRET EVER BEING ALIVE!"
"Damn."
Leon could feel the hatred pouring out of the creature. It was overwhelming.
In a strange way, both of them actually shared the same long-term goal: they both intended to kill the same god.
But Leon already understood something important.
He couldn’t allow this being to live.
The [Will of Nature] didn’t simply hate the [Goddess of Nature].
He was clearly willing to destroy the entire world if it helped him grow stronger.
Leon and this creature... Were nothing alike. Not even close.
"Alright," Leon said calmly as he nodded, "Too bad you won’t be able to do it."
"HAH?" the [Will of Nature] roared furiously. "You think YOU can stop me?!"
BOOM!
The moment he said that, the [Will of Nature] raised both of his arms into the air.
Hundreds of thick vines instantly erupted from the ground all around him, twisting violently through the air like massive spears.
The chamber trembled as the attack prepared to strike.
At that exact moment—
"Defend yourself," Leon said to Celeste without even looking back. "Your flames should be strong enough to scorch his vines. Meanwhile... I’ll deal with him."
Celeste immediately nodded. Flames burst around her body as her phoenix power ignited.
Pyra also emerged from her chest, its fiery form glowing brightly as it hovered beside her.
And as for Leon... He didn’t hesitate even for a second.
He leaned forward and launched himself across the chamber at full speed.
Straight toward the [Will of Nature].

chapters.title: Chapter 172: Leon Rushes Forward, Pyra’s New Skill
paragraphs: Leon rushed forward at full speed through the massive chamber, his eyes locked firmly on the restrained figure at the far end of the temple.
His entire focus was directed toward the [Will of Nature].
His goal was to kill it, but if it didn’t work... he knew that [Celestial’s Might] would help.
’He’s restrained, with only his arms free,’ Leon thought calmly as his body moved like a blur across the stone floor. ’This is the easiest kind of enemy to defeat... as long as I don’t mess up.’
Even so, Leon knew better than to underestimate the creature.
Just because the [Will of Nature] was partially restrained didn’t mean it was helpless.
The moment Leon began closing the distance, hundreds of vines erupted from the ground all around him, each one twisting violently through the air as they attempted to block his path.
SLASH!
Leon swung his sword in a powerful arc, cutting straight through the first vine that lunged toward him.
The blade continued moving without stopping.
Another vine tried to strike him from the side.
SLASH!
It was cut apart instantly.
The vines were incredibly sharp and extremely dangerous, but Leon’s strength had already reached a level where even attacks like these couldn’t slow him down.
Every swing of his sword carried immense force behind it. None of the vines could withstand it.
Meanwhile, Celeste had her own problem to deal with.
Several of the vines had turned their attention toward her as well, rising from the floor and whipping through the air with terrifying speed.
"Pyra," Celeste said quickly as she gripped her spear tightly, "let’s deal with them fast!"
"Kyu!"
Pyra responded immediately, flapping her small wings as flames ignited around her tiny body.
Celeste spun her spear in a defensive motion, striking several of the incoming vines and barely managing to deflect them away.
Her flames helped burn the tips of the vines, weakening them enough for her spear to push them aside.
But the attacks kept coming.
Celeste immediately began launching her abilities one after another.
Ember Ball!
A sphere of blazing fire shot forward and exploded against a vine that was about to strike her shoulder.
Flame Clone!
A duplicate made of fire appeared beside her, mimicking her movements as it swung a flaming spear at the approaching vines.
Celeste used every ability she had available.
But even with all of that... It still wasn’t enough.
SLASH!
One of the vines suddenly swung toward her from the side with incredible speed.
Celeste barely managed to react in time.
She leaned backward and dodged the attack by a hair’s breadth before jumping away to create some distance.
’Damn... this isn’t going to work,’ Celeste thought while catching her breath.
She knew her flames were strong enough to damage the vines, but there was a problem.
If the vines kept attacking like this, she would eventually run out of energy.
’I need a better way to defend myself...’
Just as she was thinking that—
"KYU!"
Pyra suddenly flapped her wings rapidly and shot upward into the air.
The small phoenix let out a powerful cry as flames gathered around her body.
Then, the little creature condensed the flames into a bright sphere before launching them downward toward Celeste.
"Huh?" Celeste blinked in confusion.
She had never seen Pyra do something like this before.
The little phoenix only had two known abilities: [Torrent of Flames] and [Flame Sense].
But what Pyra was doing now looked completely different.
The condensed flames struck the ground around Celeste and instantly spread outward.
Fwoosh!
A ring of fire erupted around her.
Then the flames rose upward, forming a protective barrier.
Flame Dome!
A dome of living fire surrounded Celeste completely.
The moment the vines tried to strike her again—
Fwoosh!
They were instantly scorched by the flames the moment they touched the barrier. None of them could get through.
Celeste’s eyes widened as she looked around at the fiery dome protecting her.
"Pyra..." she said excitedly, "you learned a new skill!"
"Kyu!"
Pyra chirped happily while flying above her.
Unlike players or natives, pets didn’t learn skills through books or scrolls.
Instead, they developed new abilities through experience, training, or specific situations. This made them incredibly versatile.
And Pyra was far from an ordinary pet. She was an ascendant-rank creature.
Even more impressive, Pyra was still only in her cub stage.
Which meant that she would become far stronger as she continued growing.
Pets evolved every ten levels. Pyra was currently level three.
That meant she only needed seven more levels before reaching her first evolution.
Once that happened, her strength would increase dramatically.
Still, the most important thing right now was that Celeste was safe.
Now that the flame dome protected her from the vines, she could finally take a moment to look toward Leon.
’I wish I could help him...’ Celeste thought quietly.
But she already knew the truth, ’I’d probably just get in his way.’
Using her flames directly on the [Will of Nature] would only burn the vines restraining him further, which could accidentally free him even more.
She had already made that mistake once. She wasn’t about to repeat it.
So instead, Celeste simply watched.
On the other side of the chamber—
Slash! Slash!
Leon continued advancing through the storm of vines.
Each step brought him closer to the restrained boss.
The vines were attacking him from every direction now, slamming into the floor, walls, and pillars as they attempted to stop him.
Leon moved with extreme precision.
He knew that even a single direct hit from one of those vines could easily kill him again.
He had already experienced how powerful they were.
And even though he technically had another [Resurrection Stone], Leon had no intention of wasting it here.
Vision Enhancement!
Leon activated his skill. Instantly, his vision sharpened.
Every movement around him became clearer.
And then—
Abyssal Slash!
Leon’s body suddenly dissolved into darkness. He vanished completely.
His shadow merged with the floor as he moved forward even faster than before.
"Where did you go, coward?" the [Will of Nature] roared as his vines slammed violently into the ground.
From the creature’s perspective, Leon had simply disappeared. But the boss wasn’t stupid.
"Alright..." the [Will of Nature] growled. "If you won’t come out... I’ll drag you out myself."
Fwoosh! BAM!
Several vines stabbed deep into the ground before glowing faintly.
They began scanning the surroundings.
Then suddenly—
"FOUND YOU!" The [Will of Nature] laughed loudly.
A massive vine crashed down toward the spot where Leon’s shadow was moving.
But Leon wasn’t concerned. He simply emerged from the darkness.
SLASH!
The attacking vine was cut cleanly in half. Leon didn’t even slow down.
’Just a few more seconds...’ he thought as he continued rushing forward. ’Just a few more...’
Slash! Slash! Slash!
The vines became even more violent as he approached the boss.
They swung faster. Harder. More aggressively. But none of it mattered.
Leon cut through every single one.
"You’re lucky I’m like this..." the [Will of Nature] growled as his glowing vine-eyes flared with green light. "Because otherwise... I would have destroyed you."
"Sure thing," Leon’s expression didn’t change at all.
For a brief moment, he even glanced backward to check on Celeste.
He immediately noticed the dome of flames surrounding her.
’I guess she found a way to defend herself,’ Leon thought with a small grin, ’Good.’
Then he turned back. With one final burst of speed, Leon dashed forward.
And in the next instant, he arrived almost directly in front of the [Will of Nature].
Leon lifted his sword.
"FOOL!" the [Will of Nature] roared.
This time, the boss didn’t attack. Instead, every vine around him rushed inward.
They twisted together, forming a massive barrier that surrounded his body completely.
The wall of vines looked incredibly thick and durable.
Leon could instantly tell that the defense was extremely strong.
But unfortunately for the [Will of Nature]... Leon had something new, an ability that he just recently learned.
He slowly raised his sword, and crimson energy began to surge around the blade.
The aura grew stronger. Then Leon unleashed his skill.
CRIMSON DANCE!

chapters.title: Chapter 173: Leon and Celeste VS Will of Nature [1]
paragraphs: As soon as Leon stepped within range of the [Will of Nature], he felt it instantly.

It wasn’t something he needed to think about or analyze in detail, but rather a sharp, instinctive awareness that told him he had reached the exact distance required to activate his new skill: [Crimson Dance].
The description had mentioned that the user needed to be close enough to the target, but it hadn’t specified the exact range.
Now that he was here, Leon could finally feel it clearly.
’So this is it...’ Leon thought as his eyes narrowed slightly while keeping his focus locked on the restrained figure ahead of him. ’The activation radius is probably around five meters.’
If he had tried to activate the skill any earlier, it likely wouldn’t have worked at all, and if he moved any closer than this, he might risk putting himself in unnecessary danger.
Right now, however, everything had aligned perfectly.
The [Will of Nature] was focused entirely on defense.
All of its vines had gathered inward, forming a massive, dense barrier around its body, clearly intending to block Leon’s attack head-on.
But that decision... Was exactly what Leon needed.
’Perfect,’ he thought calmly.
A crimson glow began to emerge from his body.
It started faintly, barely noticeable at first, but within a second it intensified rapidly, spreading across his eyes and flowing along the edge of his sword like burning energy.
The aura pulsed, and Leon could feel the power building up, concentrating itself toward a single point as if it was waiting for the exact moment to be unleashed.
And then, he swung.
His blade cut through the air in front of him, yet it didn’t strike anything physically present.
For a split second, nothing seemed to happen.
Then—
SLASH! SLASH! SLASH!
Dozens upon dozens of crimson slashes erupted all around the [Will of Nature]’s defensive barrier.
Each strike appeared instantly, as if space itself had been cut apart, and they tore through the tightly woven vines with overwhelming force.
The barrier didn’t stand a chance. The vines were shredded apart in an instant.
They were cut, split, and destroyed from every possible angle as the crimson attacks continued raining down relentlessly, leaving no room for recovery.
"Hah..." Leon exhaled, his eyes widening slightly despite himself. "Holy shit... that’s insane."
Even he hadn’t expected this level of power.
But as the final slashes faded, Leon immediately understood how the skill worked.
He didn’t need to physically reach his opponent.
As long as the target was within that radius... As long as he maintained his focus...
Every strike from [Crimson Dance] would connect. It was essentially a guaranteed hit.
An overwhelming offensive ability that allowed him to unleash dozens of attacks instantly without giving the enemy any time to react.
’That’s... broken,’ Leon thought, a faint grin forming on his face.
An ascendant-rank skill indeed deserved that kind of strength.
Still, Leon didn’t allow himself to get distracted by it for too long.
The moment the [Will of Nature]’s defensive barrier collapsed, he moved.
He dashed forward, closing the remaining distance in less than a second.
"You lose," Leon said as he appeared directly in front of the restrained figure, his sword already raised and a confident smile spreading across his face.
The [Will of Nature]’s expression twisted slightly as he looked at Leon.
"Fucking [Goddess of Nature]..." he muttered with clear hatred in his voice. "I wish she would just—
SLASH!
Leon didn’t give him the chance to finish.
His blade cut through the [Will of Nature]’s body in a clean, diagonal strike.
For a moment, everything went still. Then the body split apart.
The upper half slid slightly before collapsing, and the lower half followed shortly after, both pieces hitting the ground heavily.
Just like that... It was over.
"Damn," Leon muttered as he lowered his sword slightly, glancing at the fallen body. "I was planning to use [Celestial’s Might] first to reduce his [Combat Power]..."
He clicked his tongue lightly, "Oh well."
If this was enough to kill him, then there was no point in overthinking it. A win was a win.
Leon turned around, his attention already shifting toward Celeste as he prepared to check on her condition.
But the very instant he moved—
Fwoosh!
A massive vine suddenly appeared behind him.
This one was completely different from the others. It was thicker. And far more powerful.
"Oh."
Leon reacted immediately, raising his sword in an attempt to block the incoming attack.
But the moment the vine made contact—
BAM!
A terrifying force exploded through his body.
Even though he tried to slash it, the impact alone sent him flying backward violently, his feet leaving the ground as he was thrown across the chamber.
His body slammed against the stone floor repeatedly, bouncing once, twice, before finally sliding to a stop near the entrance of the [Temple of Nature].
"Argh..." Leon groaned as he pushed himself up quickly, wiping the blood from the corner of his mouth while staring forward. "What the hell was that..."
"Leon!"
Celeste rushed toward him immediately, stepping out of the [Flame Dome] as she looked at him with concern.
"I cut that thing in half," Leon said while keeping his eyes on the figure in the distance. "But it still attacked... be careful."
Even as he spoke, Leon could already tell something was wrong.
The vine that had just hit him... Was much stronger than the others.
Stronger to the point that even his sword hadn’t been able to cut through it cleanly.
That alone was enough to raise a red flag.
Both Leon and Celeste turned their attention forward.
And then—
"Thank you very much, human."
A voice echoed through the chamber.
"If not for you," the voice continued, "freeing myself in this state would have taken a very long time."
A chill ran through the air, "But now... I am finally free."
Leon’s eyes narrowed.
"And I can do what needs to be done."
They watched silently as the body of the [Will of Nature], the one Leon had clearly sliced in half, began to move.
The two separated halves trembled slightly.
Then, from within the severed sections, small vines and wooden tendrils began to grow.
Slowly but surely, the two halves were pulled back together, merging seamlessly as if the damage had never happened in the first place.
Within seconds... The [Will of Nature] stood whole again. As if Leon’s attack had meant nothing.
"Wow..." Celeste whispered, her eyes wide. "He... he did the same thing as you...!"
Leon didn’t respond immediately, "Hm."
So that was it. Regeneration.
The [Will of Nature] could recover from non-lethal damage entirely.
Which raised a simple but dangerous question.
If that attack hadn’t been enough to kill him... Then what would be?

"From despair... to sudden hope..." the [Will of Nature] spoke as he took a step forward, his body shifting and creaking as vines and bark moved along his form. "I must say... this is incredibly exciting."
He spread his arms wide, his expression filled with genuine joy.
He was truly enjoying this moment.
After being trapped for so long, the chance to move freely again, even slightly, was enough to fill him with excitement.
In fact, he stretched his body lightly, as if savoring the feeling of movement after ages of confinement.
"As a sign of gratitude," he continued, his tone almost polite, "your deaths will be quick."
His expression twisted into something darker.
"And they will serve as the first step toward my new glory."
He raised both arms. And in the next instant—
BOOM!
Hundreds of vines erupted from the ground across the entire chamber.
But these were not the same as before.
Each one felt as dangerous as the vine that had just sent Leon flying.
"H-Holy shit..." Celeste took a step back, her voice trembling slightly as she stared at the overwhelming scene in front of her. "This is... this is unwinnable..."
Even Pyra let out a small, nervous cry before hiding behind Celeste.
The pressure in the chamber had completely changed.
Like death was closing in from every direction.
And yet, Leon stood there. His expression didn’t change at all.
The [Will of Nature] had every reason to be confident. His [Combat Power] was at 750,000.
Leon and Celeste weren’t even close to that level.
Under normal circumstances... This fight would already be decided.
And yet, a small smile formed on Leon’s face.
"I guess the battle is fair now, I guess," he said casually.
"Huh?" the [Will of Nature] tilted his head slightly, clearly confused. "You think this is fair—"
But he stopped as his entire body suddenly trembled.
A subtle shudder ran through his form, as if something invisible had just taken hold of him.
And at that exact moment, Leon released the main passive effect of his title.
Celestial’s Might!

chapters.title: Chapter 174: Leon and Celeste VS Will of Nature [2]
paragraphs: Leon’s eyes slowly turned silvery white as he released the passive power of [Celestial’s Might].
And the moment the effect spread outward, the entire presence of the [Will of Nature] visibly reacted.
His body shuddered, as if the very core that sustained him had been forcefully suppressed.
Even the hundreds of vines surrounding him trembled in response, their movements no longer as fluid or overwhelming as they had been just moments before.
"You..." the [Will of Nature] muttered as he slowly lifted his head, the green glow within his eyes locking onto Leon with a different kind of intensity now, "...I see."
There was a brief pause. Then his expression shifted.
"You’re one of them."
At that exact moment, Leon could feel the effect of his passive fully take hold.
The overwhelming aura that surrounded the [Will of Nature] dropped noticeably, and even without needing to rely on instinct alone, the system confirmed it.
[Will of Nature (Zone Boss)]
[Combat Power: 525,000]
Still, Leon didn’t let himself relax.
Even after such a massive drop, the [Will of Nature]’s [Combat Power] remained slightly higher than his own, exceeding him by a few thousand points.
Under normal circumstances, that difference would still matter.
But right now...
’That’s good enough,’ Leon thought calmly as he tightened his grip slightly.
Before, the gap between them had been overwhelming to the point where any direct confrontation would have been borderline suicidal.
Now, however, things had changed.

"His [Combat Power] is far higher than yours," Leon said without taking his eyes off the boss, his voice steady as he spoke to Celeste. "So be careful, but your flames should be able to damage him properly."
The [Will of Nature]’s entire body was made of vines, bark, and leaves.
Which meant one thing: fire would be devastating against him.
Leon didn’t waste any time testing that assumption.
He raised his staff slightly and aimed forward.
Powerful Fireball!
A blazing sphere of fire formed instantly before shooting forward at high speed, heading straight toward the [Will of Nature].
But—
"I don’t need your flames anymore," the [Will of Nature] said calmly, his tone completely different from before as several thick vines rose up to intercept the attack.
BOOM!
The fireball exploded violently upon impact, completely destroying the vines that blocked it.
However, that also meant the [Will of Nature] himself remained unharmed.
Leon clicked his tongue lightly.
’His defense is still ridiculous,’ he thought.
The [Will of Nature] could summon vines endlessly to shield himself, sacrificing them without hesitation to block incoming attacks.
And at the same time, he possessed enough strength to fight directly if needed.
Even now, with their [Combat Power] nearly equal, this wasn’t going to be an easy fight.
’And unless I kill him instantly... he’ll just regenerate again,’ Leon thought with a faint sigh. ’That’s the real problem.’
Even a clean, fatal-looking strike hadn’t killed him before.
Which meant there had to be another condition, some kind of weakness.
’Maybe I need to restrain him completely and burn him... or maybe destroy a specific part of his body,’ Leon considered quickly, his thoughts moving fast as he analyzed the situation.
But before he could come to a proper conclusion—
"Come forth... my minions," the [Will of Nature] whispered as he slowly spread his arms outward. "Feast upon them... and grant me your strength."
Rumble...!
The ground began to shake violently.
Both Leon and Celeste immediately turned their attention outward as the area surrounding the [Temple of Nature] trembled, cracks forming across the surface as something began to emerge.
Then—
One after another, figures rose from the earth. Dozens of them.
[Nature Creature]
[Level: 75]
[Combat Power: 400,000]
[Details: Beings summoned by the "Will of Nature", every time they devour someone, the "Will of Nature" grows stronger.]
Leon’s eyes narrowed slightly as he read the panel.
’I see... so that’s how he plans to grow stronger,’ he thought, a faint grin forming on his face. ’Just devour everything in [Higher Domain #1].’
Leon doubted the [Will of Nature] would actually succeed in wiping everything out, as there were bound to be powerful players and natives capable of stopping him eventually.
But even then... The number of casualties before that point would be enormous.
"GO!" the [Will of Nature] commanded.
The [Nature Creatures] immediately began moving, rushing forward toward Leon and Celeste with overwhelming intent.
But before they could even close the distance—
"KYU!"
Pyra acted first.
Torrent of Flames!
A massive pillar of fire erupted from above, crashing down onto the battlefield with explosive force and engulfing everything in its path.
The flames consumed every single [Nature Creature] instantly.
Not only that, but the attack also struck the [Will of Nature], setting part of his body ablaze.
Leon’s eyes widened slightly as he looked up at the small phoenix hovering above.
"Nice one," he said without hesitation.
And the moment he saw the flames take effect, Leon noticed that the [Will of Nature] actually reacted slightly.
There was urgency in how he tried to extinguish the flames spreading across his body.
And more importantly, there was some fear.
’That’s it...’ Leon thought as his eyes sharpened, ’I get it now.’
He didn’t need to overthink it anymore.
All he needed to do now... Was get close enough.
Leon turned slightly.
"CELESTE!" he shouted. "Assist me with your flames!"
"Got it!" Celeste didn’t hesitate.
Now that she understood the situation better, she immediately rushed forward at full speed, her spear igniting with fire as Pyra circled above her.
Ember Ball! Flame Clone! Flame Throw!
One attack after another, Celeste unleashed everything she had, forcing the [Will of Nature] to constantly raise vines to block and defend.
The battlefield grew chaotic. Flames spread. Vines clashed against fire repeatedly.
And within that chaos, Leon advanced. Closing the distance.
"YOU WON’T KILL ME!" the [Will of Nature] roared as hundreds of vines erupted around them at once, forming a massive storm of attacks aimed directly at both Leon and Celeste.
’What do I do?!’ Celeste thought, her eyes widening as she was suddenly surrounded.
But Leon... Didn’t hesitate as he raised his staff.
Vine Cataclysm!
And in the next instant, vines erupted from the ground beneath them. HIS vines.
They surged upward violently, colliding directly with the [Will of Nature]’s attacks and deflecting them in all directions.
The two forces clashed head-on, buying just enough time.
The [Will of Nature] froze for a split second. Surprised.
And that was all Leon needed. He leaped forward.
SLASH!
His blade cut through the air as he pressed the attack.
The [Will of Nature] reacted quickly, summoning more vines to block and stall him, but Leon didn’t stop.
He moved faster. Struck again. And again. Each movement pushed him closer.
Until, he reached him. Right in front of the [Will of Nature].
"You can’t even beat me," Leon said with a small grin as he raised his sword once more. "And you think you can kill a god?"
"...SHUT UP!" The [Will of Nature] lashed out in fury.
Vine Claws!
Sharp claws formed along his arms as he swung them recklessly toward Leon, trying to tear him apart at close range.
But Leon remained composed. He dodged one strike. Parried another. Deflected a third.
Their movements clashed rapidly, each exchange happening within fractions of a second as they fought at close range.
For a brief moment... They were equal. Or at least, it seemed that way.
Until the [Will of Nature] finally noticed it: there was a faint crimson glow forming along Leon’s blade once again.
CRIMSON DANCE
Leon swung. And instantly—
Dozens of crimson slashes erupted around the [Will of Nature], striking from every direction at once and cutting through his body relentlessly.
There was no escape. The attacks tore through him completely.
His form was shredded apart. Everything was cut into pieces.
The remains collapsed to the ground.
"FOOL..." the [Will of Nature] muttered as his severed head rolled slightly, his glowing eyes still fixed on Leon. "I’m immortal!"
"Sure you are," Leon replied with a calm grin as he lifted his staff once more.
Powerful Fireball!

chapters.title: Chapter 175: The Will of Nature’s Weakness, 9 Levels In A Row?
paragraphs: The moment Leon finished unleashing [Crimson Dance] and cut the [Will of Nature] into dozens of scattered pieces, he didn’t relax or assume the fight was over, because his eyes immediately caught something important.
The vines that made up the creature’s body... Were moving.

Even after being completely torn apart, the pieces didn’t stay still for more than a second before small tendrils began stretching outward, slowly crawling toward one another as if guided by an invisible force that refused to let the body remain separated.
They were trying to fuse again.
Trying to restore the [Will of Nature] like nothing had happened.
But Leon didn’t move back. He didn’t hesitate.
And he definitely didn’t give it the chance.
Powerful Fireball
He raised his staff instantly, gathering flames at the tip before launching the attack directly toward the scattered remains.
BOOM!
The fireball exploded upon impact, sending flames spreading across every piece of the [Will of Nature]’s body, scorching the vines, the bark, and the fragments that were still trying to reconnect.
And this time, it worked.
"ARGH...!"
A pained roar erupted from the severed head lying on the ground as the vines recoiled violently, their movements breaking apart as the fire burned through them.
The tendrils that had been reaching toward each other shriveled under the heat.
The regeneration stopped for now.
’Knew it,’ Leon thought with a grin as he watched the reaction carefully. ’Fire stops the regeneration.’
Without fire, the [Will of Nature] could endlessly recover from anything, but with fire burning through its body, the regeneration process was interrupted entirely.
Which also meant something else.
Anyone without fire-based attacks... Would lose this fight.
Leon briefly considered that there might be another hidden method to deal with the boss, perhaps some kind of core or specific weak point, but at this stage, he didn’t need to overthink it.
He already had the solution.
"YOU!"
Fwoosh!
Several thick vines suddenly erupted from the ground around Leon, moving defensively as they tried to shield the burning pieces of the [Will of Nature].
Now that its regeneration had been halted, the boss could actually die.
But that also meant it would do everything it could to prevent the flames from continuing.
Because if the fire went out... It would recover again.
The design of this opponent was clear.
As long as it wasn’t burned continuously, it was effectively immortal.
It was no wonder the [Goddess of Nature] didn’t kill him.

"It’s because she couldn’t," the [Will of Nature] suddenly laughed, even in its current state, its voice echoing with a strange mix of pride and bitterness. "The [Goddess of Nature] tried again and again... until she realized that trapping me was far more efficient."
That explained everything. Because killing it outright... Wasn’t easy.
But now—
Slash!
Leon stepped forward and cut into the head again, slicing through it to further damage the structure, yet even as he did, the flames from his previous attack were already beginning to fade.
"Futile!" the [Will of Nature] roared. "YOU CAN’T KILL ME!"
And just like that, as the fire weakened, the vines began moving again.
Slowly at first. Then faster. The regeneration was restarting.
Leon’s expression tightened slightly as he observed the process, but there was no panic in his eyes.
He had already figured it out.
"Celeste, Pyra," Leon called out as he turned toward them, his voice firm and direct. "Burn this guy, quickly."
He could already see the torso and limbs beginning to reconnect, while smaller vines extended toward the head, trying to reattach it to the rest of the body.
If they didn’t act now... It would recover again.
"Got it!" Celeste didn’t hesitate for even a moment.
She rushed forward alongside Pyra, both of them immediately unleashing everything they had.
Ember Ball!
A blazing sphere shot forward, launching a stream of fire toward the [Will of Nature]’s body.
Torrent of Flames!
At the same time, Pyra let out a sharp cry as a massive pillar of fire erupted, engulfing every scattered piece of the boss in an overwhelming inferno.
ROOOOAR!
A deep, primal roar echoed through the chamber as the flames consumed him.
This time, the reaction was even stronger than before.
The fire didn’t just interrupt the regeneration. It suppressed it completely.
Leon stepped back slightly alongside Celeste as the pillar of flames continued burning, watching carefully as the entire area turned black and scorched from the intensity.
’Pyra’s flames are the strongest among us,’ Leon thought with a faint grin. ’And they last longer too.’
That made all the difference.
Because even after the main pillar of fire began to fade... The ground remained burning.
The pieces of the [Will of Nature] were still engulfed in lingering flames.
The only sound that came from the boss now was weak and strained, far from the overwhelming presence it had before.
It was on the verge of death. But even then... Leon didn’t relax.
Because he knew something important.
If he didn’t finish it right now... It would still recover.
And so—
Abyssal Slash!
Leon’s body dissolved into shadows as he moved instantly, slipping through the ground and rushing toward the severed head while avoiding the lingering flames.

"Wait...!" the [Will of Nature] suddenly spoke, its voice urgent now, the green glow in its eyes flickering as it tracked Leon’s movement beneath the surface. "We both seek to kill the [Goddess of Nature]... let us become allies!"
Leon didn’t respond. He had already made up his mind.
Fwoosh!
He emerged from the shadows directly in front of the head, his sword raised and infused with dark energy.
And as he looked down at it, he noticed something.
The green glow inside its eyes... Wasn’t just light. It felt like something more.
And so—
"Nah," Leon said with a faint smile.
He swung.
SLASH!
The blade cut cleanly through the head, splitting it in half while the darkness-infused energy shattered whatever lay within the glowing core.
The light flickered. Then, it began to fade.
"Then..." the [Will of Nature] muttered weakly, its voice breaking apart as its consciousness slipped away. "We... both... die..."
And just like that, it ended.
The presence that had filled the chamber vanished completely.
Fwoosh! Ding!
[You have killed "Will of Nature (Zone Boss)" and gained 3,500,000 experience points.]
[100% Drop Rate has triggered...]
"Phew..." Leon exhaled as a grin spread across his face. "That was incredible."
The amount of experience alone was insane.
It was easily the highest he had gained in this life so far.
And since Celeste had contributed heavily to the fight, she received the same reward.
Even Pyra gained a portion of it.
Ding!
[Congratulations, you have leveled up to Level 57 + Level 58 + Level 59 + ... + Level 65!]
[Due to "Heaven’s Blessing", you have gained 3,600 points in all attributes and 3,600 free points to distribute.]
Leon let out a small laugh as he looked at the panel.
Celeste had also leveled up significantly, reaching level 67, while Pyra climbed up to level 5.
All three of them had grown stronger from this battle.
Everything had increased. It was a massive gain.
For a moment, Leon relaxed slightly, his mind already shifting toward checking his [Storage Space].
But just as he was about to do that—
Ding!
Another panel appeared in front of him.
This one was different. It was completely green.
Its border was wrapped in twisting vines, and a faint skull symbol rested at the center.
Leon’s expression stilled slightly as he read it.
[You have been afflicted with the "Will of Nature’s Curse"]
"Oh."

chapters.title: Chapter 176: The Will of Nature’s Curse, Double Experience Points?!
paragraphs: Ding!
[You have been afflicted with the "Will of Nature’s Curse"]
The instant the panel appeared before Leon, his eyes narrowed slightly.
Without wasting even a second, he turned his head toward Celeste, who stood a short distance away and was already looking through her own panels with a focused expression.
"Did you receive the curse just now?" Leon asked urgently, though he still kept himself composed.
"What?" Celeste blinked in confusion as she quickly skimmed through everything in front of her before she shook her head, "...No? What’s that about a curse?"
There was a visible concern in her voice as she spoke, but Leon simply nodded once before shifting his gaze back toward the panel hovering in front of him.
The fact that he was the only one affected by it made things immediately clear in his mind.
There was no randomness involved in something like this, meaning the [Will of Nature] had deliberately targeted him in its final moments.
’So much for wanting to kill the [Goddess of Nature], huh,’ Leon thought with a quiet sigh.
Curses were not something unfamiliar to him as he heard of some in his past life.
They were the opposite of blessings, which in contrast helped players.
Curses were meant to slow players down, restrict their abilities, or place them in situations that made progression significantly more difficult.
And because of that, they were almost always considered devastating.
In fact, in the vast majority of cases, a curse was something that could practically seal a player’s fate.
The effects could range from constant poisoning, to the complete inability to use magic or physical strength, to even more complex and restrictive conditions.
Leon’s expression darkened ever so slightly as these thoughts passed through his mind.
Though the change was brief and quickly disappeared as he let out a quiet breath and shook his head.
"Oh well," he muttered calmly.
There was no point in dwelling on it, and more importantly, there was nothing he could do to avoid it now that it had already been applied.
So instead, Leon chose to face it directly.
With that, he focused his gaze and opened the curse’s panel.
[Curse: Will of Nature]
[Description: You have been cursed by the "Will of Nature" for stopping him on his way to become stronger, and as a result, he shall hinder your growth as well.]
[From now on, you will require twice as many experience points to level up, and the experience points increase per level is also doubled.]
For a brief moment, Leon simply stared at the description as if making sure he had read it correctly.
And then almost immediately, his attention shifted toward his status panel.

However, the moment the effect of the [Will of Nature’s Curse] fully took place, the panel began to change right before his eyes, as thin vines spread across it and tightened around the numbers like they were alive.
Ding!
"Wow."
The amount of experience required to level up had been doubled instantly.
And considering that each level previously increased the requirement by 20,000 experience points, it now meant that the increase would jump to 40,000 instead.
The intention behind the curse was obvious.
The [Will of Nature] had sought to leave the [Temple of Nature] and grow stronger at a rapid pace by devouring others.
And in contrast, it had chosen to slow Leon’s growth as much as possible in retaliation for being stopped.
It was a simple and effective form of revenge.
And yet... Leon smiled.
"This is... the best possible curse," he said with a light laugh, "Incredible."
If anyone else had received this curse, their reaction would have been completely different.
Doubling the experience required to level up was essentially the same as cutting their progression speed in half, which would normally be devastating.
But Leon was in a completely different situation.
Because of his [Celestial] title, he was forced to choose [Yes] a choice appeared.
Meaning that he couldn’t delay his advancement even if he wanted to.

Once he reached level 100, he would be forced into his final assessment before entering the [Eternal Domain], and that was something he had been concerned about, as he knew he might not be fully prepared when that moment came.
However, with this curse in place, everything changed.

By doubling the experience required to level up, Leon would naturally take much longer to reach level 100, effectively giving him more time to grow stronger, gather resources, and prepare himself for what was ahead.
In other words, what was supposed to be a restriction had become an advantage.
"Anyone else would be cursing their luck right now," Leon continued with a faint grin as he glanced toward the remains of the [Will of Nature], "but this actually works perfectly for me."
He then brought up the panel again and quickly sent it over to Celeste so she could see it for herself.
The moment she read through the description, her eyes widened slightly as she let out a soft gasp.
But then, as she thought about it a little more, her expression shifted.
"Wait a minute," she said as realization dawned on her, "doesn’t that mean you’ll have more enemies to use your talent on?"
"Bingo," Leon replied with a satisfied grin, clearly pleased that she had come to the same conclusion, "a curse like that would have worked on you too."
"Wow!" Celeste’s eyes sparkled with excitement.
Her [Phoenix Ember] talent allowed her to grow stronger by consuming defeated enemies.
And if her leveling speed was slowed down, it would naturally give her more opportunities to use that talent before reaching higher levels.
Celeste even felt sad that she hadn’t been cursed.
Without wasting any time, she turned toward the scorched remains of the [Will of Nature].
She approached the massive corpse that was still smoldering from the flames.
Fwoosh!
As she activated her talent, flames erupted from her body and spread toward the remains, quickly engulfing them as they burned intensely for a brief moment before seeping into her.
Ding!
[Your "Phoenix Ember" has consumed a zone boss.]
[+20 Strength, +40 Constitution, +15 Agility.]
"Hehe."
A small, satisfied smile appeared on her face as she felt the increase in her strength.
Even though she hadn’t received any items from the boss itself, her talent more than made up for it.
Meanwhile, Leon shifted his attention toward his own rewards as he opened his [Storage Space] and began to review everything he had obtained from the fight.
[Will of Nature Essence: Consuming will increase Constitution by 250, Strength by 150, Agility by 100.]
[Will of Nature Gloves (Mythical): +3,000 Attack, +1,700 Strength, +1,400 Constitution, +1,000 Agility.]
[Sub-Talent Scroll: Mega Constitution Enhancement (A-Level)]
[Skill Stones x30]
[Enhancement Stones x25]
[Elemental Skill Stone (Mythical): Using this will upgrade two of your element-related skills by one level as long as the skills are below level 5.]
"Damn."
The amount of items he acquired from the [Will of Nature] was indeed formidable.
The journey to the [Temple of Nature] had proven to be extremely rewarding, and this final haul only solidified that fact.
He could already feel that his power was about to increase by a noticeable margin once he started using these items properly.
And combined with the effects of the curse, it felt like everything had aligned in his favor.
Yet just as he was about to start organizing everything and deciding what to use first...
Ding!
A new system panel appeared before both of them.
[Players "Celestial" and "UndyingPhoenix" have managed to conquer the "Temple of Nature" and kill the "Will of Nature"]
[You have been awarded 50 Reputation Points.]

chapters.title: Chapter 177: 500 Reputation Points, Celestial Token
paragraphs: Ding!
[Your reputation has reached 500, you will now gain 50 additional attributes per level.]
Leon let out a long breath as the panel appeared before his eyes, his lips slowly curling into a satisfied grin while he took in the words carefully.
"Good," he muttered under his breath.
He had more or less expected this outcome, especially after everything they had just accomplished inside the [Temple of Nature].
After all, much like when he reached 250 reputation points, 500 was also a big milestone.
Still, despite being satisfied with that part, his attention quickly shifted to what came next.
’I hope I get another stat increase,’ Leon thought with a faint grin, already imagining how broken it would be if his attributes per level increased again.
He’d actually be more than satisfied with just that, as it would make his [Combat Power] skyrocket.
Without wasting any time, he focused on the panel that appeared for his milestone reward.
Ding!
[You have obtained the "Celestial Token"]
And... that was all.
Leon blinked once, "...Wait, what?"
His expression didn’t change much, but the confusion was obvious in his eyes as he stared at the single line of text in front of him.
He expected something more to appear... but nothing did.
Just... that. The [Celestial Token].
For a brief moment, Leon almost felt like complaining, because compared to what he had imagined, this seemed... underwhelming.
But just as that thought crossed his mind, he suddenly stopped himself.
’Hold on.’ Leon wasn’t stupid.
There was no way the system would give him something worse than what he had received at 250 reputation, especially when this milestone was clearly more important.
Which meant that the value of the [Celestial Token] simply wasn’t obvious at first glance.
Much like the [Divine Key] or [Tower of Souls Token], it had to have a special use that could make it incredibly powerful.
This... felt exactly like that kind of item.
Without hesitation, Leon opened the item’s panel.
[Celestial Token (???): A token that every Celestial receives at 500 Reputation Points, will be extremely important in the future.]
[Note: if you lose it, you die.]
"...Damn."
Leon let out a quiet breath as he read through the description, his eyes narrowing slightly as he processed the information.
It didn’t explain much. In fact, it explained almost nothing.
But the few details it did provide were more than enough to make him take it seriously.
The fact that every Celestial received this token meant that it wasn’t just some random item.
And the second line... If you lose it, you die.
’I guess I’ll see,’ Leon thought as he closed the panel, his expression returning to normal.
What caught his attention even more, however, was the mention of "every Celestial."
This meant that beside him, the 199 other celestials also received this thing at 500 Reputation Points.
Leon’s gaze drifted slightly as he thought about it.
Since he was [Celestial Being #200], that meant everyone before him had started earlier, progressed further, and were most likely far stronger than he currently was.
Would he meet them eventually? Would they be allies? Enemies?
Leon didn’t have the answer, but one thing was certain: they wouldn’t be weak.
"Hm..." Leon scratched the side of his chin for a moment before letting out a small sigh, deciding not to overthink it for now, "Whatever."
He stored the [Celestial Token] inside his [Storage Space], making sure it was secure before shifting his focus back to the present.
If 500 reputation gave him this, then 750 would probably be more interesting.
And just as that thought crossed his mind—
Ding!
[Your "Blood Heart" has recharged.]
"Oh?"
Leon’s eyes widened slightly before a grin spread across his face almost instantly.
Now that... was something he had been waiting for.
In fact, he didn’t even need to wait a single second to use it.
Without hesitation, Leon focused on it, feeling his heartbeat slowly synchronize with the artifact as a faint crimson energy began to pulse through his body.
Ding!
[You have used the "Blood Heart" on the "Divine Armor"]
[You have blessed the "Divine Armor"]
Fwoosh!
The golden armor he was wearing suddenly changed as crimson streaks spread across its surface, glowing faintly as a new power settled into it.
Leon immediately opened the panel to check the result.
[Divine Armor (Ascendant): +10,000 Defense, +5,000 Spirit, +5,000 Strength, +4,000 Agility, +3,000 Constitution.]
[Blood Heart Blessing: You are completely immune to all light and darkness-related attack.]
Leon tilted his head slightly as he read the effect, his expression thoughtful rather than excited.
"Not as good as the others."
Compared to some of the previous blessings he had received, this one felt a bit more situational, but that didn’t mean it was useless.
Immunity to two entire types of attacks was still incredibly strong, especially if he ever faced enemies that relied heavily on light or darkness.
So in the end, Leon simply nodded, "It’ll do."
Once he was done with that, he turned his gaze toward Celeste, who had been quietly watching him the entire time.
She didn’t seem impatient or bothered at all, just waiting for him to finish.
"Go ahead," she said with a small smile. "No need to rush."
"Thanks," Leon replied with a nod before turning back to his [Storage Space].
He quickly pulled out the [Will of Nature Essence] and consumed it without hesitation.
Nom! Ding!
[+250 Constitution, +150 Strength, +100 Agility.]
A wave of power surged through his body as the stats were added, making him feel slightly stronger almost instantly.
Then, without wasting time, he removed his [Shadow Gloves (Epic)] and replaced them with the [Will of Nature Gloves (Mythical)], the difference in quality obvious the moment he equipped them.
After that, he stored the [Enhancement Stones] and [Skill Stones] for later use, deciding that now wasn’t the time to spend them.
And then...
"Here."
Leon casually tossed the [Mega Constitution Enhancement (A-Level)] scroll toward Celeste.
She caught it instinctively, her eyes widening the moment she saw what it was.
"Wow..." she whispered, clearly amazed. "This is insane..."
Leon simply smiled.
He already had that sub-talent, and while he could have tried to upgrade it further, Celeste would benefit from it far more than he would.
Making her stronger... was just as important.
And finally, Leon’s attention shifted to the last item he had left: the [Elemental Skill Stone (Mythical)].

chapters.title: Chapter 178: Using The Elemental Skill Stone
paragraphs: [Elemental Skill Stone (Mythical): Using this will upgrade two of your element-related skills by one level as long as the skills are below level 5.]
Leon gazed at the stone’s description one last time to fully understand how it worked, and a wide grin spread on his face.
"Amazing," he muttered under his breath, his tone filled with genuine satisfaction.

Out of everything the [Will of Nature] had dropped, this was easily the best item he had received, and aside from the [Will of Nature’s Curse], which had its own strange advantages, this might actually be the most impactful reward he had gotten from the entire fight.
Without wasting any more time, Leon immediately opened his skills panel, wanting to see exactly what he was working with before deciding how to use the stone.

[Skills: Appraisal (Common Lv.5), Vision Enhancement (Common Lv.4), Powerful Fireball (Common Lv.6), Storm of Lightning (Elite Lv.4), Crescent Slash (Epic Lv.2), Darkness Barrier (Epic Lv.2), Abyssal Slash (Legendary Lv.3), Blood Beam (Legendary Lv.1), Celestial Hand (Ancient Lv.2), Ice Spikes (Legendary Lv.1), Vine Cataclysm (Legendary Lv.1), Crimson Dance (Ascendant Lv.1)]
"Hm."
Leon couldn’t help but notice something right away.
Despite having a wide variety of skills across multiple ranks, most of them were still at relatively low levels, far lower than what he actually wanted them to be.
With his [100% Drop Rate] talent, getting [Skill Stones] should have been much easier compared to other players, but the truth was that he simply hadn’t focused on that aspect yet.
He had been moving forward constantly, fighting stronger enemies, clearing dangerous zones, and chasing bigger opportunities, which meant that upgrading his skills had taken a bit of a backseat.
’Soon,’ Leon thought calmly, his eyes narrowing slightly as he looked at the panel, ’Very soon.’
Once he started focusing on upgrading his skills properly, his overall strength would increase significantly, even if his [Combat Power] didn’t directly reflect it.
Higher-level skills often gained new effects, improved efficiency, or completely changed how they worked, which meant that investing in them was always worth it.
Out of curiosity, Leon quickly checked his [Storage Space] to see how many [Skill Stones] he had accumulated so far.
[Skill Stones x50]
"Not bad," he said quietly, though his tone didn’t sound particularly impressed, "but not that good either."
For most players, having fifty [Skill Stones] would already be considered an incredible amount, enough to significantly upgrade multiple abilities.
But for Leon, it still felt lacking. He wanted hundreds.
Still, it was more than enough to work with for now.
Looking back at his skill list, Leon quickly identified which abilities were eligible for the [Elemental Skill Stone].
Since the stone only worked on element-related skills that were below level 5, that narrowed down his options.
[Storm of Lightning], [Darkness Barrier], [Blood Beam], [Ice Spikes], and [Vine Cataclysm].
Among those, the first choice was obvious.
Fwoosh!
Leon poured his mana into the [Elemental Skill Stone], and as it began to glow faintly in his hand, a panel appeared before him.
Ding!
[Which skill do you wish to upgrade (2/2 uses left)]
"Storm of Lightning." There was no hesitation in his voice.
The skill was already at level 4, meaning that upgrading it to level 5 would normally cost a large number of [Skill Stones], so using the stone on it was the most efficient choice.
Ding!
[You have upgraded "Storm of Lightning (Level 4)" to "Torrent of Lightning (Level 5)"]
"Nice."
Leon immediately opened the updated skill panel.
[Torrent of Lightning (Elite Lv.5): Focus your Spirit and condense it into a torrent of lightning that can hit multiple targets in a wide area and possibly stun them.]
The description hadn’t changed much, but Leon could already tell that the actual power behind the skill had increased significantly.
Stronger damage, wider range, better effects. Exactly what he wanted.
Now, he had one more use left. His gaze shifted to the remaining options.
’Either [Blood Beam], [Ice Spikes], or [Vine Cataclysm],’ he thought, carefully considering each one.
All three were [Legendary]-rank and sitting at level 1, which meant they had a lot of room to grow.
But among them...
"Vine Cataclysm it is," Leon decided with a small nod.
However, instead of using the [Elemental Skill Stone] immediately, he paused for a moment.

chapters.title: Chapter 179: The Goddess of Nature’s Introduction, Small Rest Before Domain Travel
paragraphs: Meanwhile...
Garden of Eden, Eternal Domain.
Ding!
[The "Will of Nature" has been killed by "Celestial"]

A soft voice echoed through a vast, peaceful landscape filled with endless flowers swaying gently under a calm breeze, as a tall figure resting on a bed of blooming petals slowly lifted her gaze toward the panel that had just appeared before her.
Her expression remaining composed, almost indifferent, as if nothing in the world could truly disturb her state of mind.

She was breathtakingly beautiful, with long golden hair cascading down her back like sunlight itself, her features delicate yet flawless, and her entire presence surrounded by a serene aura that felt both comforting and overwhelmingly powerful at the same time.
"The... [Will of Nature]?" she murmured quietly, her tone thoughtful as she tried to recall something that sounded so distant it almost felt irrelevant.
For a moment, she genuinely didn’t remember. It had been too long.
Too many years had passed since that name held any meaning to her.
But after a few seconds, something clicked.
"Oh... that thing," she said with a faint grin forming on her lips, as if she had just remembered something trivial, "Too bad, I guess."
Her reaction was casual, almost dismissive, completely opposite to the intense hatred that the [Will of Nature] had harbored toward her for so long.
To him, she had been everything. The one he wanted to destroy and surpass.
The one he had spent years raging against while trapped in the [Temple of Nature].
And yet, to her... He was barely worth remembering.
All that hatred, all that anger... had been entirely one-sided from the very beginning.
The figure who had spoken those words was none other than the [Goddess of Nature] herself.
[Elowen, The Goddess of Nature].

The place she resided in, the [Garden of Eden], was her personal domain within the [Eternal Domain], a space that existed solely for her, shaped entirely by her will, where she could do whatever she pleased without restriction.
Slowly, Elowen rose from the bed of flowers, the petals shifting gently beneath her as she stood, her height reaching around two meters, her presence both elegant and overwhelming.
Everything she wore was made from nature itself.
Her dress was woven from vibrant flowers that never wilted.
Her sandals were formed from living vines that wrapped softly around her feet.
And above her head floated a delicate halo made of small glowing plants, radiating a faint, natural light.
She was the very embodiment of nature.
And yet... undeniably dangerous.
Because beneath that serene appearance was still a god.
And like all gods... she was capable of cruelty beyond comprehension, willing to do anything to achieve her goals, no matter the cost.
"My garden has been doing quite well lately," Elowen said softly as she stretched her arms slightly, her voice calm and satisfied, "Only a few more years... and it might finally be ready."
Her words carried a strange weight, as if she was preparing something far greater than what could be seen on the surface.
But her attention didn’t remain there for long.
Instead, her gaze returned to the panel that had appeared earlier.
More specifically... to the name displayed within it.
"Celestial..." she whispered, her eyes narrowing ever so slightly as a spark of interest appeared within them, "Is it actually another one of them?"
There was a brief pause as she thought about it, her expression slowly shifting into something more intrigued.
"If that’s the case... then that would make them number 200."
A wider smile formed on her face as that realization settled in.
"...Which means they’re all here now."
There was something unsettling about the way she said it, as if this was something she had been waiting for.
"Heh..." she chuckled softly, her tone filled with quiet amusement. "I guess I won’t be telling the others.
Rather than reacting with concern or urgency, Elowen simply sat back down on her bed of flowers.
Her posture relaxed as her glowing eyes reflected countless thoughts and possibilities unfolding within her mind.
Around her, several plant-like creatures moved about.
Some were small, almost cute in appearance, with soft glowing leaves and gentle movements.
Others were massive, towering beings made of thick vines and bark, their presence far more intimidating.
They surrounded her like loyal pets, reacting to her emotions as if they could feel her thoughts.

"Calm down, my children," Elowen said gently as she extended her arms, trying to embrace as many of them as she could at once, her smile never fading, "I’m sure that very soon... you’ll be able to eat as much as you want."
There was a faint glint in her eyes as she spoke, something dark hidden behind her otherwise gentle demeanor.
Back to Leon and Celeste.

The two of them stood once again inside the [Will of Nature’s Attack Zone], having just exited the [Temple of Nature], their surroundings returning to the familiar sight of countless vines slowly moving across the area.
Despite the boss being defeated, the environment itself hadn’t changed.
The vines were still alive.
"Wait," Celeste said as she looked around, her brows furrowing slightly in confusion, "we killed the [Will of Nature], so how are these still here?"
Leon glanced around calmly before answering, his tone steady as always.
"Because it obviously wasn’t the [Will of Nature] that was stopping people from entering the [Ancient Gate] in the first place."
"Huh?" Celeste blinked, clearly not following. "Then who was it?"
Leon didn’t hesitate, "The [Goddess of Nature]," he replied.
Celeste froze for a moment, her eyes widening in shock, "A... goddess?!"
Her reaction was completely normal.
After all, beings like gods weren’t something most players even knew about at this stage.
Even Leon, in his past life, hadn’t learned about them until much later.
"She probably placed all of this here herself," Leon continued calmly. "Though I doubt she even remembers doing it."
That alone said enough.
To a god, something like sealing the [Will of Nature] and surrounding it with deadly vines was likely nothing more than a minor action, something not even worth remembering over time.
Still, Leon’s gaze shifted toward the [Ancient Gate].
And then—
CRACK!
Small cracks suddenly appeared across its surface.
Until it shattered completely, breaking apart and disintegrating into nothingness.
"...Well," Leon shrugged slightly, "guess there’s no reason for this place to exist anymore."
Now that the [Will of Nature] was gone, the purpose of the gate had disappeared along with it.
But deep inside, Leon’s expression turned cold for just a brief moment.
’Don’t worry... [Goddess of Nature],’ he thought silently, ’I’ll get to you eventually.’
"Is she evil?" Celeste asked after a moment, still processing everything she had just heard. "The [Goddess of Nature], I mean."
"Yes," Leon replied instantly, without even thinking. "No mercy if we ever see her, or any other god for that matter."
He paused briefly before adding,
"Though right now... we’re nowhere near strong enough."
Celeste nodded slowly, absorbing that information.
"Wow... alright."
Even with their current strength, they were still insignificant compared to gods.
But that didn’t mean they would stay that way.
As long as they kept growing stronger, that gap would eventually shrink.
"How many gods are there?" Celeste asked curiously as she noticed Leon opening his [World Map].
Leon shrugged, "No idea. Maybe a hundred. Maybe more. Doesn’t really matter."
He wasn’t trying to avoid the question. He genuinely didn’t know.
And even if he did... it wouldn’t change anything.
"Hold on to me," Leon said with a small smile.
Celeste immediately grabbed his hand.
Ding!
[Do you wish to teleport to "Divine Academy City"?]
"Yes."
Fwoosh!
In an instant, the two of them disappeared and reappeared just outside the city.
They quickly made their way inside, blending into the busy environment filled with players and natives moving about.
"We can rest for a few hours," Leon said as they walked. "At least until [Domain Travel] resets."
"Yay~!" Celeste beamed. "I want to try a restaurant or something!"
"Deal," Leon replied with a grin.
After wandering around for a bit, they found one of the most crowded places in the area, clearly a popular spot.
It took them around thirty minutes to get a table, but once they were finally seated—
"I want EVERYTHING," Celeste declared to the server without hesitation.
Leon couldn’t help but laugh.
"Bring everything," he added.
The server hesitated for a moment before nodding nervously, "A-Alright..."
About twenty minutes later, dozens of plates filled the table, covering it completely with food of all kinds.
Celeste’s eyes sparkled as she stared at it.
"Do all phoenix-race individuals eat this much?" Leon asked with a smile.
"I don’t think so," Celeste said, blushing slightly. "But I’m special, so... let’s enjoy this!"
"Sure," Leon sighed, amused.
It took her an entire hour to finish everything.
Leon only ate a bit here and there, mostly watching in mild disbelief as she somehow managed to consume it all.
At one point, she even summoned Pyra to help eat, before sending her back again.
Once they were done, Leon paid for everything, which barely affected his balance, and they left.
"We still have around five hours," Leon said. "We can rest at an inn."
They quickly found one near the [Divine Academy] and got a room.
As soon as they entered—
"You can sleep," Leon said. "I’ll wake you up when the cooldown ends."
"Alright, thanks!" Celeste smiled.
Fwoosh!
"Kyu!"
She summoned Pyra again, and the two of them quickly fell asleep together.
Leon, on the other hand, sat quietly at the edge of the bed, his gaze calm but thoughtful.
’Well...’ he thought with a faint grin, ’things are going well for now...’
But even then...
’I still need to be careful.’

Leon only ate a bit here and there, mostly watching in mild disbelief as she somehow managed to consume it all.
At one point, she even summoned Pyra to help eat, before sending her back again.
Once they were done, Leon paid for everything, which barely affected his balance, and they left.
"We still have around five hours," Leon said.
"We can rest at an inn."
They quickly found one near the [Divine Academy] and got a room.
As soon as they entered—
"You can sleep," Leon said.
"I’ll wake you up when the cooldown ends."
"Alright, thanks!" Celeste smiled.
Fwoosh!
"Kyu!"
She summoned Pyra again, and the two of them quickly fell asleep together.
Leon, on the other hand, sat quietly at the edge of the bed, his gaze calm but thoughtful.
’Well...’ he thought with a faint grin, ’things are going well for now...’
But even then...
’I still need to be careful.’

chapters.title: Chapter 180: I’m The Weakest Celestial?
paragraphs: While Celeste and Pyra rested peacefully on the inn’s bed, their breathing calm and steady after the battle, Leon remained seated at the edge.
His posture was relaxed but his mind still fully active as he decided to take advantage of the quiet moment to review everything he had gained so far.
Moments like these were rare and he knew that staying ahead required constant awareness of his own strength.
He slowly opened his status panel, and the familiar interface appeared before his eyes, displaying everything about him in clear detail.
[Name: Leon Rykard]
[ID: Celestial]
[Talent: 100% Drop Rate (SSS)]
[Slaughter Meter: 798/1000 (Tier-3)]
[Titles: Celestial Being #200, Reputable, Slayer III, Life Vessel]
[Curse: Will of Nature]

[Sub-Talents: Mega Constitution Enhancement (A-Level), Supreme Strength Enhancement (S-Level), King of Darkness (S-Level), Super Agility Enhancement (B-Level), Supreme Spirit Enhancement (S-Level), Intermediate Necromancy (C-Level), Strong Poison Resistance (B-Level), Blood Monarch (S-Level), Master of Elements (SS-Level), Deep Light Affinity (B-Level)]
[Constitution: 18,175 (+32,675)]

[Skills: Appraisal (Common Lv.5), Vision Enhancement (Common Lv.4), Powerful Fireball (Common Lv.6), Torrent of Lightning (Elite Lv.5), Crescent Slash (Epic Lv.2), Darkness Barrier (Epic Lv.2), Abyssal Slash (Legendary Lv.3), Blood Beam (Legendary Lv.1), Celestial Hand (Ancient Lv.2), Ice Spikes (Legendary Lv.1), Vines of Torment (Legendary Lv.5), Crimson Dance (Ascendant Lv.1)]
[Unique Skill: Divine Answer (???)]
[Forbidden Skills/Spells: Oblivion Meteor]
[Free Points to Allocate: 7,450]
[Eternal Coins: 516,470]
[Reputation Points: 500]
A wide grin slowly spread across Leon’s face as he stared at the numbers in front of him, because seeing his progress laid out so clearly made everything feel real.
And more than anything, it reminded him just how far he had come compared to his previous life.
Back then, at this same level, he had been nowhere near this strong, not even remotely close.
If the version of himself from the past were to stand in front of him now, the fight would end in less than a second without any exaggeration.

His stats had risen to absurd levels, each one boosted heavily by his sub-talents and equipment, and when combined with his skills, his overall [Combat Power] had reached a point that most players wouldn’t even dream of at level 65.
"Yeah... this is good," Leon muttered quietly to himself, clearly satisfied.

With everything taken into account, including his [Master of Elements] sub-talent and the variety of abilities he had access to, Leon estimated that he could comfortably take on enemies with around 700,000 Combat Power, which was insane considering his actual level.
Still, even with all of that, he didn’t allow himself to relax too much.
Strength like this wasn’t enough, not for what was coming.
His gaze slowly shifted toward the bed, where Celeste was sleeping peacefully with Pyra curled up beside her, the small phoenix letting out soft sounds as it rested.
Leon’s expression softened slightly.
’They need to get stronger too,’ he thought.

It wasn’t just about him anymore, because if they were going to face gods and whatever else stood beyond the higher domains, then Celeste and Emilia would need to reach that level as well, or at the very least get close enough to survive.
After that, Leon returned his attention to his panel and noticed something else.
[Free Points to Allocate: 7,450]
"That’s... quite a lot," he admitted with a small chuckle.
He had been postponing allocating them for a while now, focusing more on immediate combat and growth instead of optimization, and it had resulted in this large accumulation.
Still, he didn’t feel any urgency.
’I’ll deal with it later,’ he thought, shrugging lightly.
There was no need to rush, especially since his current stats were already more than enough for now.
Then his eyes moved to another section.
[Eternal Coins: 516,470]
"Nice."
The number was significantly higher than before, which meant that the items he had listed in the [Trading House] had most likely sold successfully, bringing in a steady flow of income.
Overall, everything was going smoothly.
Leon then shifted his focus to his equipment, mentally reviewing each piece he had equipped.
Weapons:
[Power Sword +2 (Mythical): +15,000 Attack Power, +7,000 Strength, +3,500 Agility. Requirement: Complete the "Orc Trial of Strength"]
[Blood Heart Blessing: Every attack with this sword holds double the "Strength" of a usual one.]
[Void Staff +3 (Mythical): +2,500 Spirit. Requirement: Level 15.]
[Blood Heart Blessing: The "Spirit" bonus of the staff is tripled.]
Head:
[Plant King Flower (Legendary): +1,000 Agility, +1,500 Constitution, +1,300 Strength. Equipping this item will prevent the vines of the "Will of Nature’s Attack Zone" from attacking you.]
[Magic Necklace (Legendary): +500 Spirit.]
[Elemental Necklace (Mythical): Boosts the power of elemental attacks by 25%.]
[Toxic Snake Scales (Rare): +200 Constitution.]
Body:
[Divine Armor (Ascendant): +10,000 Defense, +5,000 Spirit, +5,000 Strength, +4,000 Agility, +3,000 Constitution.]
[Blood Heart Blessing: You are completely immune to all light and darkness-related attack.]
[Silk Belt +2 (Epic): +350 Defense, +150 Constitution, +200 Agility.]
[Vine Boots +2 (Elite): +1,500 Agility, +1,000 Constitution.]
[Will of Nature Gloves (Mythical): +3,000 Attack, +1,700 Strength, +1,400 Constitution, +1,000 Agility.]
"Yeah... this is solid," Leon nodded quietly.
Every single piece contributed significantly to his overall power, and combined with his abilities, it created a build that was both offensive and durable.
After finishing his review, Leon leaned back slightly and allowed himself to relax for a brief moment.
Without much hesitation, he reached into his [Storage Space] and pulled out two items.
The [Primordial Dragon of Chaos Egg] and the [Celestial Token].
The egg appeared on the ground in front of him, completely still, its surface pulsating with an almost imperceptible energy.
Leon glanced at its status.
[Hatching Time: 4,228 years, 326 days.]
"...Right."
He couldn’t help but let out a quiet sigh.
Seeing Pyra and how she interacted with Celeste had definitely made him more interested in hatching his own pet, especially one that sounded as absurd as a primordial dragon of chaos.
He could already imagine what kind of power it might possess once fully grown.
Still...
’No idea how to reduce that time,’ he thought.

At this point, he would have to start actively searching for a solution once he reached [Higher Domain #3] and reunited with Emilia, because otherwise, he might eventually be forced to use one of his limited [Divine Answer] uses just to figure it out.
After a moment, Leon shifted his attention to the second item: the [Celestial Token].
He spun it lightly between his fingers, observing its surface as he tried to interact with it, pouring a bit of mana into it to see if it would react.
At first... nothing happened.
Then suddenly—
Beep!
A small panel appeared in front of him.
[Not worthy yet, it is not the right time.]
Leon’s eyes widened slightly, "Oh... so it does something."
Curious, he tapped it again. Another panel appeared.
[You are "Celestial Being #200", the last one.]
[Current Rank: 200/200]
"Damn..."
Among all the celestials, Leon was currently ranked last. The weakest.
Still, instead of being bothered by that, he simply smirked.
’Makes sense,’ he thought calmly.
He had been the last to become a [Celestial], so naturally, the others would be far ahead in terms of progress and power.
But that didn’t matter. Not in the long run. Soon enough, he would surpass them all.
And when that happened... things would get interesting.
The next few hours passed quietly, with Leon eventually closing his eyes to rest while summoning three [Undead Skeletons] to stand guard around the room, ensuring that nothing would disturb them.
Time flowed peacefully until—
Ding!
[Domain Travel’s cooldown has ended, you can use it again.]
