I’m not going in there."
"If it was [Hell], maybe..."
"Let’s just wait and see what happens."
And just like that, the idea died.
No one followed.
Instead, they chose to stay behind, watching, waiting, curious to see whether the so-called [Celestial] could actually conquer something like this.
Meanwhile, inside the portal...
Leon felt his body being pulled apart and reassembled at the same time, the space around him twisting violently as he was transported into the [Hellish Beach].
The sensation lasted only a few seconds.
But it was enough.
Fwoosh!
Leon landed.
His feet sank slightly into warm sand as the sound of waves crashing echoed in the distance.
He slowly lifted his gaze.
Behind him, a dense forest stretched outward, its trees dark and twisted.
And far ahead...
A massive volcano towered over the entire landscape, smoke rising from its peak as faint red light pulsed from within.
’I guess that’s where the boss is,’ Leon thought with a small grin forming on his lips.
He turned around, already speaking.
"Emilia, Celeste, do you guys see this—"
But he suddenly stopped as he realized that he was the only one around.
Neither Celeste nor Emilia were close to him at this moment.
"Oh," Leon let out quietly.
It seemed...
They hadn’t been sent to the same spawn point.
Since [Realms] were much larger than [Zones], they didn’t function the same way when it came to entry points.
Instead of sending every player to a fixed location, they were designed with multiple spawn points scattered across the entire map.
Making exploration more unpredictable and forcing players to adapt rather than rely on coordination from the very start.
That also meant that even if a group entered together, or even if someone followed right behind another person, there was no guarantee they would appear anywhere close to each other.
In fact, more often than not, they wouldn’t.
’I guess I’ll have to find them myself,’ Leon thought calmly as he began to move forward, not showing any sign of concern despite the situation.
To him, this wasn’t really a problem.

Even though the name of the realm was [Hellish Beach], Leon quickly realized that the beach itself was only a small portion of the entire area, most likely serving as an outer layer or starting zone for players entering the realm.
The real challenge clearly lay deeper within.

The island itself stretched far beyond the sandy shore, and the massive forest ahead seemed to be the true beginning of the journey, acting as the main path players would have to cross before even getting close to the volcano.
To Leon, none of this really changed his approach.
Whether it took hours or days didn’t matter to him.
As long as he could complete the quest, that was enough.
Even if it meant spending multiple days inside this realm, grinding enemies, collecting drops, and slowly making his way forward, he was completely fine with it.
In fact, part of him even welcomed it.
After all, he still needed to level up, and more importantly, he needed items.
And this place...
It was perfect for that.
Not to mention, he still had to wait for the cooldown of his [Life Vessel] title to reset, which meant that staying here for a while wasn’t a bad idea at all.
But just as he was about to step into the forest...
Leon suddenly stopped.
His expression shifted slightly.
’Actually...
I just thought of something.’
Searching for Celeste and Emilia blindly across an entire island wasn’t exactly efficient, especially considering how large this realm seemed to be.
And even if they all moved toward the volcano, there was no guarantee they would meet quickly.
And while that wasn’t a major issue...
It was still annoying.
He had already received messages from both of them, likely asking about his location or checking if he was alright.
But instead of replying immediately, Leon decided to try something else.
Something that might make things much easier.
"World Map."
The moment he said it, a familiar panel appeared before his eyes, expanding outward and displaying a large, detailed interface.
This was the first time he was using the [World Map] inside a [Realm] or [Zone], and he wasn’t entirely sure how it would behave.
But...
If it worked the way he hoped...
Then things would become much simpler.
And a second later, the map appeared.
Leon’s eyes lit up slightly as he looked at it.
The entire [Hellish Beach] island was displayed before him, meaning that the [World Map] indeed worked on it!
Though not everything was visible: large portions of the map were covered in a grey fog, clearly indicating unexplored areas.
Which meant that the system only revealed locations that the player had either visited or had visual access to.
Still...
That was more than enough.
Because now, Leon could clearly see his own position.
A small marker representing him was placed right on the beach, exactly where he was standing.
And ahead of him was the forest.
But more importantly...
At the center of the island, the volcano stood out clearly on the map, marked with a distinct symbol: a skull.
’I guess it’s showing me where the boss is too,’ Leon thought with a grin, clearly satisfied.
But that wasn’t even the best part.
Because just a moment later, he noticed two small dots moving.
"They’re here," Leon muttered under his breath.
Celeste and Emilia.
Each of them was visible on the map.
But they weren’t close.
Not even slightly.
They had been spawned on completely different sides of the island, far apart from each other, which only confirmed just how large this realm truly was.
Still, that didn’t matter anymore.
Because now, Leon knew exactly where they were.
And more importantly...
They knew where to go.
Without wasting any time, Leon opened his messages and quickly sent one to both of them.
[Celestial: I can see you on the "World Map", just do whatever you want, I’ll find you eventually.]
The reply came almost instantly.
[Saintess: Alright ٩(◕‿◕)۶]
[UndyingPhoenix: I’ll be waiting for you!]
Leon smiled faintly as he closed the panel.
Everything was under control.
There was no need to rush.
They could all move at their own pace, grow stronger, and eventually meet up somewhere along the way.
And with that...
Leon finally stepped forward.
The sand beneath his feet shifted slightly as he moved, the sound of the waves slowly fading behind him as he approached the edge of the forest.
Leon’s grin slowly returned.
"Let’s see what this [Hellish Beach] is really about."
And with that, he stepped into the forest.

chapters.title: Chapter 189: The Pyroman Apes
paragraphs: Leon stepped deeper into the tropical forest of the [Hellish Beach], his grip steady on both his staff and sword as his eyes scanned everything around him with sharp focus.
Despite the ominous name of the realm and the fact that he had chosen the [Nightmare] difficulty without hesitation, the first impression the place gave him was surprisingly peaceful.
’If not for the fact I knew this was a [Realm], this could actually pass as some kind of vacation spot,’ Leon thought with a faint grin forming on his lips as he walked forward.
The trees around him were tall and lush, their leaves forming a thick canopy that filtered the sunlight into soft beams.
While the ground beneath his feet was covered in patches of grass and roots that seemed perfectly normal, almost too normal considering where he was.
Even the air felt clean at first, carrying a slight tropical warmth that would have been relaxing under different circumstances.
More importantly, Leon didn’t encounter a single monster.
He continued walking for several minutes, his senses constantly active, but nothing happened.
’Did we actually enter the [Nightmare] difficulty?’ he wondered silently, his eyes narrowing slightly.
The current situation didn’t match the expectations he had for the hardest difficulty of a realm that was supposedly feared by so many players.
But just as that thought settled in his mind, things began to change.
It wasn’t immediate, and it wasn’t obvious at first.
However, after around ten minutes of walking deeper into the forest, Leon finally noticed something that didn’t belong.
Some of the trees around him were scorched.
The bark was blackened, cracked, and in some places still faintly smoking, as if the damage had been done not long ago.
And the leaves on those trees were either completely burned away or hanging weakly, barely clinging to life.
Leon slowed down slightly as his gaze shifted from one tree to another.
And the further he walked, the more frequent they became.
Even the ground itself started to change, with patches of dirt turning darker, while small cracks appeared here and there, emitting faint traces of warmth.
’The volcano, I guess?’ Leon raised his eyebrows slightly.
But even then, something didn’t quite add up.
This didn’t feel like natural damage. It felt... intentional.
And only a few minutes later, Leon finally found the answer.
A faint crackling sound reached his ears.
At first, it blended with the ambient noise of the forest, but as he focused on it, the sound became clearer, sharper, unmistakable.
Something was burning.
Leon immediately shifted his direction, moving toward the source of the sound with controlled speed, his body low and ready in case he needed to react instantly.
And when he arrived...
"What the hell?"
The sight in front of him made him pause for a brief moment.
A group of monkeys, sturdy in build and standing upright, were scattered across a small clearing.
Each one holding a torch as they actively set fire to the surrounding trees, bushes, and even the ground itself, completely indifferent to the destruction they were causing.
Flames spread rapidly across the area, devouring everything in their path while thin streams of lava-like cracks snaked across the ground.
Leon immediately activated his skill.
Appraisal!
[Pyroman Ape]
[Level: 75]
[Talent: Flame Affinity (C-Level)]
[Combat Power: 450,000]
[Details: A group of monkeys tasked to burn down anything they see, they enjoy the sight of fire burning things.]
But among the group, one stood out.
Its entire body was covered in flames, and its presence alone felt more dangerous than the rest combined.
Its eyes were glowing with an aggressive intensity that made it clear it wasn’t just another member of the group.
[Mega Pyroman Ape (Mutated)]
[Level: 75]
[Talent: Deep Flame Affinity (B-Level)]
[Combat Power: 500,000]
[Details: A pyromane ape that mutated by being constantly exposed to fire.]
The moment Leon finished reading the panels, the group of pyroman apes turned toward him almost at the same time.
And then, they locked onto him.
The [Mega Pyroman Ape] reacted first, stepping forward aggressively as it raised its massive torch and brought it close to its mouth.
Flame Blow!
In a single motion, it exhaled forcefully, and the flames from the torch erupted outward, expanding instantly into a massive wave of fire that swallowed the entire area in front of it.
Leon didn’t move.
The flames hit him directly, engulfing his entire body in a blazing inferno that lasted for several seconds, burning everything in its path.
"Kakaka!"
"Kaka!"
The apes erupted into excited noises, clearly enjoying the sight as they watched the flames consume what they believed was another victim.
Their expressions were almost gleeful as they anticipated the aftermath.
But then... The flames faded.
And Leon was still standing there. Completely unharmed.
The reason was simple: [Master of Elements].

With his affinity toward fire, not only were his own fire-based attacks significantly stronger, but his resistance to fire itself had reached a level where attacks like these were practically meaningless against him.
And considering the difference in [Combat Power] between them... There was never any real threat.
Leon didn’t say anything. He simply raised his staff.
Powerful Fireball!
A condensed sphere of fire formed instantly at the tip of his staff before being launched forward at high speed.
BOOM!
The explosion that followed was violent and overwhelming, instantly consuming the group of pyroman apes and wiping them out without giving them any chance to react.
All of them. Except one: The [Mega Pyroman Ape].
It survived. Barely.
Its body was heavily damaged, flames flickering unevenly as it staggered backward, clearly realizing that the human in front of it was far beyond anything it could handle.
And in that moment... It made its decision.
Fwoosh!
Without even attempting to fight back, the mutated ape turned around and dashed into the forest at incredible speed, using its agility and knowledge of the terrain to escape as quickly as possible.
Leon blinked once, slightly surprised.
’Didn’t expect that.’
Most enemies would choose to fight until the end.
But this one... It knew when it was outmatched. And it chose survival.
But unfortunately for it, that wasn’t going to work.
’This is exactly why I like spells,’ Leon thought as he lifted his staff once more, his expression calm as he focused his energy.
The air around him began to buzz. The atmosphere shifted.
Even the sky above seemed to dim slightly as energy gathered, crackling with intensity.
Torrent of Lightning!
ZAP! ZAP! ZAP!

Multiple bolts of lightning descended from above, striking the ground in rapid succession as they chased the fleeing [Mega Pyroman Ape], forcing it to constantly change direction as it tried to avoid the attacks.
For a moment it worked.
The ape dodged several strikes, narrowly escaping death each time as the lightning hit the ground around it.
But it didn’t last as one bolt struck it.
ZAP!
It hit the ape directly, sending a surge of electricity through its body and stunning it instantly, freezing it in place as its muscles locked up.
That was enough to seal its fate.
Leon moved.
In a single swift motion, he closed the distance between them, his sword already raised as he reached the stunned creature.
And then—
SLASH!
The blade cut cleanly through its neck. The [Mega Pyroman Ape] didn’t even have time to react.
Its head separated from its body instantly, and it collapsed to the ground, lifeless.
Ding!
[You have killed x5 "Pyroman Ape" and gained 250,000 experience points.]
[You have killed "Mega Pyroman Ape (Mutated)" and gained 150,000 experience points.]
[100% Drop Rate has triggered...]
Leon didn’t even have time to process everything before another notification appeared.
Ding!
[Congratulations, you have leveled up to Level 66!]
[Due to "Heaven’s Blessing", you have gained 450 points in all attributes and 450 free points to distribute.]
A grin immediately spread across his face.
"Well, I guess the [Will of Nature]’s curse is working just fine," Leon said as he looked at the notification with clear satisfaction.
If this had been before the curse, with his previous experience requirements, this fight alone would have easily pushed him up two, maybe even three levels without any difficulty.
But now it only gave him one. And yet, Leon didn’t mind.
If anything, he preferred it this way. More opportunities to grow stronger that way.
He quickly glanced at his updated status.
"Damn," he muttered under his breath, noticing the increased requirement for the next level.
He didn’t care that much about it though, and so he opened his [Storage Space], his interest immediately shifting toward the items he had just obtained.

chapters.title: Chapter 190: The Hellish Beach’s Drops, Immune to Fire?
paragraphs: [Pyroman Ape Essence x5: Consuming will increase Agility by 8 and Spirit by 10.]
[Mega Pyroman Ape Essence: Consuming will increase Agility by 13 and Spirit by 15.]
[Sub-Talent Scrolls: x5 Flame Affinity (C-Level); Deep Flame Affinity (B-Level)]
[Pyroman Ape Fur x6 (Rare): +1,000 Constitution, +500 Spirit. Increased resistance to fire-related attacks.]
"Nice," Leon nodded with a satisfied grin as he reviewed everything that had dropped, clearly pleased with the outcome of such a quick encounter.
Especially considering how effortlessly he had handled the group despite it being a [Nightmare] difficulty [Realm].
He didn’t hesitate for even a second after that.
Nom!

Without overthinking it, Leon immediately consumed all the essences one after the other, letting the energy flow through his body as his stats steadily increased, the familiar sensation of growth spreading across his limbs and mind.
Ding!
[+53 Agility, +65 Spirit.]

Even though the numbers themselves didn’t seem that impressive at first glance when compared to his already massive stats, Leon knew very well that this kind of incremental growth was exactly what made the difference in the long run.
Especially when stacked over dozens or even hundreds of similar gains, which would eventually turn into a noticeable boost.
"Still worth it," he muttered under his breath, already thinking ahead.
He casually stored the sub-talent scrolls into his [Storage Space] without even considering using them.
They were completely unnecessary for him at this point, especially with his [Master of Elements] sub-talent already pushing his fire affinity far beyond what those scrolls could offer.
Then, his attention shifted toward the [Pyroman Ape Fur].
Without wasting time, Leon immediately began fusing them together.
Ding! Ding!
[Enhancement successful x2.]
Beep!
[Enhancement failed.]
Ding! Ding!
[Enhancement successful.]
Leon raised his eyebrows slightly as the results came in, clearly not expecting such a good outcome.
Yet he couldn’t complain in the slightest as he ended up with a significantly improved item.
[Pyroman Ape Fur +3 (Rare): +2,000 Constitution, +1,300 Spirit. High resistance to fire-related attacks.]
"That’s better," he said calmly.
He equipped the fur around his neck right away, removing the [Toxic Snake Scales (Rare)] he had been using previously without any hesitation.
The new item was simply superior in every aspect, especially considering the environment he was currently in.
The moment the fur settled around his neck, Leon could feel a faint warmth spreading across his body.
But unlike the oppressive heat of the environment, this one felt controlled and almost comforting.
He took a moment to observe his surroundings again.
’Alright...’

The ground around him had become even more unstable than before, with cracks spreading in every direction and faint traces of lava glowing beneath the surface, while the heat in the air continued to intensify with every step he took deeper into the island.
Leon summoned the [World Map] once again, his eyes quickly scanning the layout.
The volcano still stood far in the distance, towering over everything else, its presence dominating the entire island.
"If it already looks like this from this far away..." Leon muttered thoughtfully, "then getting close to that thing is probably going to be a whole different problem."
It became increasingly clear that reaching the boss wouldn’t be as simple as just walking straight toward it.
For most players, staying near the outer areas of the forest and farming weaker monsters would likely be the safer and more efficient option.
But Leon had no intention of doing that.
At the same time, he noticed something else on the map: both Emilia and Celeste were moving.
Emilia’s position didn’t concern him at all, as her durability and overall strength were more than enough to handle anything this place could throw at her, but Celeste...
Leon narrowed his eyes slightly.
Her [Combat Power] was around 420,000, which meant that while she was strong, she wasn’t overwhelmingly stronger than the enemies here.
That meant there was still some level of risk involved.
She wouldn’t die permanently, of course, but even a single death would result in a loss of precious time and experience points.
And in a place like this, that could slow them down significantly.
Not to mention the uncertainty regarding the quest itself.
If she died, would she still be considered part of the quest? Or would the system treat it as a failure?
That was something Leon didn’t want to test.
Then there was Pyra. This [Realm] was practically perfect for her growth.
If she could reach level 10 here, she would undergo her first evolution, which would likely boost her strength significantly and provide Celeste with even more support.
Leon quickly sent a message.
[Celestial: I’ll try to head toward you, Celeste, just make sure not to take too many risks.]
A short pause followed. Then, the reply came.
[UndyingPhoenix: I got jumped by a group of "Pyroman Apes", but I’m completely immune to fire!]
Leon blinked once. Then... realization hit him.
"Oh, of course.’

If Celeste was naturally immune to fire, whether because of her race or her talent, then the majority of the enemies in this [Hellish Beach] wouldn’t be able to harm her at all using their primary attacks.
That changed things completely.
It meant that only physical attacks or stronger abilities could pose a real threat to her.
Leon let out a small breath.
"I guess I underestimated her a bit," he admitted quietly.
Still, even with that in mind, he had no intention of leaving her alone for too long.
At the very least, meeting up again would make everything more efficient.
’Those affinity sub-talents are going to be perfect for her,’ he thought with a slight grin, already planning ahead, ’I should collect as many as I can.’
Leon shifted his focus back to the present. His expression hardened slightly as he looked forward.
Celeste and Emilia were moving. So was he. Eventually, their paths would cross again.

He made sure to keep the [World Map] open as he continued forward, watching as more of the greyed-out areas slowly revealed themselves with each step he took, gradually uncovering the true scale of the island.
It was massive. Large enough that fully mapping it out would likely take an entire day, if not more.
But that didn’t bother him.
As long as he knew where he was, and where the others were, that was more than enough.
Everything else was secondary.
"Time to farm properly," Leon said with a faint grin.
Before long, he came across another clearing. This one was far more intense than the previous area.
The trees were completely engulfed in flames, the ground beneath them cracked and glowing, while the air itself shimmered with heat.
And in the center of it all... More enemies.
Several [Pyroman Apes], along with a group of [Fire Hobgoblins], all gathered together as if guarding the area.
Leon’s expression didn’t change in the slightest. He simply raised his staff.
Torrent of Lightning!
The air around him began to crackle violently as energy gathered above, the sky darkening slightly as multiple lightning strikes formed in an instant before descending toward the enemies.
ZAP! ZAP! ZAP!
The strikes hit with overwhelming force, spreading across the entire clearing and instantly eliminating most of the weaker monsters, while the rest were left stunned and barely standing.
"GRRRAAH!"
The [Fire Hobgoblins] were the only ones that managed to endure the attack to some extent, their bodies resisting the damage as they broke free from the stun with visible effort.
Their skin, glowing faintly with heat, made them far more durable than the others.
Leon narrowed his eyes slightly.
’A good armor piece might drop from them,’ he thought, already considering the possibilities, ’Celeste could definitely use an upgrade if it’s better than what she’s wearing.’
Even in the middle of combat, Leon was not only thinking about himself, but also his companions.
’I also wanted to test my new ability...’
Leon adjusted his grip on his staff slightly. Then, without hesitation, he activated another skill.
Vines of Torment!

He didn’t hesitate for even a second after that.
Nom!

Without overthinking it, Leon immediately consumed all the essences one after the other, letting the energy flow through his body as his stats steadily increased, the familiar sensation of growth spreading across his limbs and mind.
Ding!
[+53 Agility, +65 Spirit.]

Even though the numbers themselves didn’t seem that impressive at first glance when compared to his already massive stats, Leon knew very well that this kind of incremental growth was exactly what made the difference in the long run.
Especially when stacked over dozens or even hundreds of similar gains, which would eventually turn into a noticeable boost.
"Still worth it," he muttered under his breath, already thinking ahead.
He casually stored the sub-talent scrolls into his [Storage Space] without even considering using them.
They were completely unnecessary for him at this point, especially with his [Master of Elements] sub-talent already pushing his fire affinity far beyond what those scrolls could offer.
Then, his attention shifted toward the [Pyroman Ape Fur].
Without wasting time, Leon immediately began fusing them together.
Ding!
Ding!
[Enhancement successful x2.]
Beep!
[Enhancement failed.]
Ding!
Ding!
[Enhancement successful.]
Leon raised his eyebrows slightly as the results came in, clearly not expecting such a good outcome.
Yet he couldn’t complain in the slightest as he ended up with a significantly improved item.
[Pyroman Ape Fur +3 (Rare): +2,000 Constitution, +1,300 Spirit.
High resistance to fire-related attacks.]
"That’s better," he said calmly.
He equipped the fur around his neck right away, removing the [Toxic Snake Scales (Rare)] he had been using previously without any hesitation.
The new item was simply superior in every aspect, especially considering the environment he was currently in.
The moment the fur settled around his neck, Leon could feel a faint warmth spreading across his body.
But unlike the oppressive heat of the environment, this one felt controlled and almost comforting.
He took a moment to observe his surroundings again.
’Alright...’

The ground around him had become even more unstable than before, with cracks spreading in every direction and faint traces of lava glowing beneath the surface, while the heat in the air continued to intensify with every step he took deeper into the island.
Leon summoned the [World Map] once again, his eyes quickly scanning the layout.
The volcano still stood far in the distance, towering over everything else, its presence dominating the entire island.
"If it already looks like this from this far away..." Leon muttered thoughtfully, "then getting close to that thing is probably going to be a whole different problem."
It became increasingly clear that reaching the boss wouldn’t be as simple as just walking straight toward it.
For most players, staying near the outer areas of the forest and farming weaker monsters would likely be the safer and more efficient option.
But Leon had no intention of doing that.
At the same time, he noticed something else on the map: both Emilia and Celeste were moving.
Emilia’s position didn’t concern him at all, as her durability and overall strength were more than enough to handle anything this place could throw at her, but Celeste...
Leon narrowed his eyes slightly.
Her [Combat Power] was around 420,000, which meant that while she was strong, she wasn’t overwhelmingly stronger than the enemies here.
That meant there was still some level of risk involved.
She wouldn’t die permanently, of course, but even a single death would result in a loss of precious time and experience points.
And in a place like this, that could slow them down significantly.
Not to mention the uncertainty regarding the quest itself.
If she died, would she still be considered part of the quest?
Or would the system treat it as a failure?
That was something Leon didn’t want to test.
Then there was Pyra.
This [Realm] was practically perfect for her growth.
If she could reach level 10 here, she would undergo her first evolution, which would likely boost her strength significantly and provide Celeste with even more support.
Leon quickly sent a message.
[Celestial: I’ll try to head toward you, Celeste, just make sure not to take too many risks.]
A short pause followed.
Then, the reply came.
[UndyingPhoenix: I got jumped by a group of "Pyroman Apes", but I’m completely immune to fire!]
Leon blinked once.
Then... realization hit him.
"Oh, of course.’

If Celeste was naturally immune to fire, whether because of her race or her talent, then the majority of the enemies in this [Hellish Beach] wouldn’t be able to harm her at all using their primary attacks.
That changed things completely.
It meant that only physical attacks or stronger abilities could pose a real threat to her.
Leon let out a small breath.
"I guess I underestimated her a bit," he admitted quietly.
Still, even with that in mind, he had no intention of leaving her alone for too long.
At the very least, meeting up again would make everything more efficient.
’Those affinity sub-talents are going to be perfect for her,’ he thought with a slight grin, already planning ahead, ’I should collect as many as I can.’
Leon shifted his focus back to the present.
His expression hardened slightly as he looked forward.
Celeste and Emilia were moving.
So was he.
Eventually, their paths would cross again.

He made sure to keep the [World Map] open as he continued forward, watching as more of the greyed-out areas slowly revealed themselves with each step he took, gradually uncovering the true scale of the island.
It was massive.
Large enough that fully mapping it out would likely take an entire day, if not more.
But that didn’t bother him.
As long as he knew where he was, and where the others were, that was more than enough.
Everything else was secondary.
"Time to farm properly," Leon said with a faint grin.
Before long, he came across another clearing.
This one was far more intense than the previous area.
The trees were completely engulfed in flames, the ground beneath them cracked and glowing, while the air itself shimmered with heat.
And in the center of it all...
More enemies.
Several [Pyroman Apes], along with a group of [Fire Hobgoblins], all gathered together as if guarding the area.
Leon’s expression didn’t change in the slightest.
He simply raised his staff.
Torrent of Lightning!
The air around him began to crackle violently as energy gathered above, the sky darkening slightly as multiple lightning strikes formed in an instant before descending toward the enemies.
ZAP!
ZAP!
ZAP!
The strikes hit with overwhelming force, spreading across the entire clearing and instantly eliminating most of the weaker monsters, while the rest were left stunned and barely standing.
"GRRRAAH!"
The [Fire Hobgoblins] were the only ones that managed to endure the attack to some extent, their bodies resisting the damage as they broke free from the stun with visible effort.
Their skin, glowing faintly with heat, made them far more durable than the others.
Leon narrowed his eyes slightly.
’A good armor piece might drop from them,’ he thought, already considering the possibilities, ’Celeste could definitely use an upgrade if it’s better than what she’s wearing.’
Even in the middle of combat, Leon was not only thinking about himself, but also his companions.
’I also wanted to test my new ability...’
Leon adjusted his grip on his staff slightly.
Then, without hesitation, he activated another skill.
Vines of Torment!

chapters.title: Chapter 191: Testing Vines of Torment, The Hellish Hobgoblin [1]
paragraphs: Leon had already tested [Torrent of Lightning] against the monsters of the [Hellish Beach], and the results had been more than satisfying, especially now that the skill had reached level five.
It made its damage, range, and overall impact far more devastating than before, allowing him to wipe out entire groups of enemies with ease while barely putting in any effort.
However, that wasn’t the skill he was interested in right now.
The other ability he had upgraded using the [Elemental Skill Stone] was the one that truly caught his attention: [Vines of Torment].
[Vines of Torment (Legendary Lv.5): Your vines seek nothing but death and agony, they will emerge from the ground and destroy anything in their way, leaving none of them standing.]
Even just reading the description again made Leon raise his eyebrows slightly, as it had clearly changed compared to before, becoming far more aggressive and violent in tone.
It was something meant to annihilate now.
Leon knew something very important though: using vines against fire-based enemies was, in most situations, a terrible idea.
That was common sense. But that was exactly why he decided to test it here.

If this skill could perform well even against enemies that naturally countered it, then that would mean its true potential was far greater than expected, especially when used against opponents that didn’t have any resistance to this type of attack.
And so, without hesitation...
Fwoosh!
Leon activated the skill. The effect was immediate.
The atmosphere around him shifted, the air growing heavier as a dark presence spread across the clearing.
And at the same time, the ground beneath his feet began to tremble violently as if something massive was about to break through.
Cracks formed. The earth split open. And then...
BOOM!
Dozens of vines burst out from the ground all at once, erupting with terrifying force.
Leon’s eyes widened slightly as he observed them. They were completely different from before.

Each vine was now at least twice as thick, their surface darker, almost black, and covered in countless sharp thorns that glistened faintly in the fire-lit surroundings, giving them a much more menacing appearance than anything he had previously summoned.
They didn’t look like ordinary vines anymore.
The moment the [Fire Hobgoblins] saw them, something changed in their expressions.
Instinct kicked in. They understood that they were about to die.
And so, without hesitation...
"HRAAAH!"
All four remaining hobgoblins roared loudly toward the sky, their voices echoing through the burning clearing.
At first, Leon assumed it was nothing more than a final, desperate cry, something they did when they realized escape was no longer possible.
But he didn’t dwell on it. Because at the same time...
SNATCH!
The vines moved.

They shot forward at incredible speed, wrapping around the nearby monsters before they could react, tightening instantly and crushing them with overwhelming force, snapping bones and tearing through bodies without giving them any chance to resist.

Even though many of these creatures had fire-based bodies, the vines held firm, their durability far exceeding what Leon had expected, resisting the ambient heat and pressure of the environment with ease.
Still, Leon knew that direct fire attacks would likely burn them if given enough time.
But that didn’t matter. Because the enemies never got that chance.
The clearing was being wiped out in seconds.
And now... The final four vines moved.
They surged forward toward the group of [Fire Hobgoblins] that had roared earlier, aiming to finish them off just like the others.
Everything seemed to be going exactly as Leon expected.
Until—
ROOOOOAR!
A deafening roar suddenly exploded through the area.
The sound that made the air vibrate and sent a chill down Leon’s spine even in the middle of intense heat.
Leon’s eyes widened instantly.
SLASH!
Before the vines could reach their targets, something massive moved.
In a single motion, all the vines that had been rushing toward the hobgoblins were cut apart, shredded into pieces as if they were nothing more than fragile threads.
Leon looked up. And for the first time since entering the clearing...
"What the hell..."
[Hellish Hobgoblin (Boss)]
[Level: 75]
[Sub-Talents: Super Strength Enhancement (B-Level), Deep Flame Affinity (B-Level)]
[Combat Power: 660,000]
[Details: Roams the "Hellish Beach" realm seeking anybody who is unlucky enough to encounter him.]

Standing before him was a massive figure, easily over four meters tall, its body radiating heat as flames flickered across its skin, while in its hands it held a giant burning bat, its sharp teeth visible through its mouth.
Leon didn’t realize it immediately, but he had just encountered one of the biggest reasons why this realm was feared.
Not simply because of the powerful monsters or the environment, but this thing was one of them.
An entity strong enough to wipe out entire groups of players on its own.
And yet... Leon didn’t look particularly worried. Instead, he slowly adjusted his stance.
’Our combat power is close enough,’ he thought calmly, analyzing the situation, ’I should be able to fight it head-on and win if I play this right.’
The [Hellish Hobgoblin] stared at him. But instead of attacking immediately...
ROOOOOAR!
It roared again. Even louder than before.
The sound spread across the entire island, echoing through the forest, the beach, and even reaching distant areas.
Far away, Celeste and Emilia both froze for a brief moment as they heard it.
Their expressions changed instantly. They didn’t hesitate as they quickly sent messages to check on each other.
[Saintess: What the hell was that?]
[UndyingPhoenix: Even the monsters I’m fighting reacted to it... that was insane!]
Leon glanced at the messages briefly, then looked back at the boss in front of him.
His expression twitched a little, knowing that this thing was strong.
This wasn’t going to be a simple fight.
And more importantly... [Celestial’s Might] wasn’t going to activate here. He would have to rely entirely on himself.
At the same time, the [Fire Hobgoblins] that had been on the verge of death moments ago suddenly regained their confidence.
With their leader present, their fear disappeared almost instantly.
They were no longer prey. They were hunters again.
Fwoosh!
Leon didn’t wait. He raised his staff!

chapters.title: Chapter 192: The Hellish Hobgoblin [2]
paragraphs: Multiple spells were cast in rapid succession, each one heading straight toward the enemies with overwhelming force.
The hobgoblins reacted immediately, fear flashing across their faces once again.
But before the attacks could reach them—
THUMP!
The boss moved. With a single step forward, the [Hellish Hobgoblin] intercepted everything.
It blocked the fireball head-on, raised its body to shield the others from the lightning, and swung its massive bat to shatter the incoming ice spikes before they could make contact.
Leon’s eyes narrowed.
’Damn... it’s protecting them.’
He had expected to thin out the weaker enemies first while dealing with the boss separately.
The boss seemed to be arrogant, but it wasn’t going to let them die easily.
Leon shifted his stance slightly, preparing to engage directly.
But then—
RUMBLE! RUMBLE!
The ground began to shake again. This time though, it wasn’t from his skill.
Leon’s expression changed slightly as he looked around, a bad feeling rising in his chest.
The vibrations were getting stronger. Closer. As if something was approaching.
No... Not something. Many things.
He looked back at the boss. And for the first time... It was smiling.
A wide, twisted grin spreading across its face as if everything was going exactly as it had planned.
The rumbling intensified. Dozens of footsteps. Maybe more. All rushing toward the clearing at the same time.
"Human... die... soon," the boss said slowly, its voice rough and broken, yet filled with clear intent.
It was taunting him. Even if its speech was crude, the meaning was obvious.
Leon stared at it for a moment. Then, he let out a quiet breath.
"We’ll see about that, goblin" he replied calmly, tightening his grip on his weapon as the sounds of approaching enemies grew louder and louder.
Fwoosh!
Leon dashed forward at full speed, not even bothering to wait and figure out what exactly was rushing toward him from all sides.

Because in a situation like this, hesitation was the worst possible option, and if something dangerous was approaching, then the best move was to take control of the fight before it escalated further.
Abyssal Slash!

Without slowing down, Leon activated his movement skill, his body sinking into the darkness beneath his feet as he attempted to reposition instantly and gain an advantage over the [Hellish Hobgoblin].
But the moment he entered the ground... He came right back out.

’HOT!’ Leon’s eyes widened as he immediately canceled the movement, his body reappearing above the surface with a sharp intake of breath, clearly caught off guard by what he had just felt, ’Damn it...!’
The underground wasn’t normal terrain. It was filled with intense heat and molten energy, almost like layers of lava flowing beneath the surface.
And even with his high fire resistance, that didn’t mean he could casually move through something like that without taking damage.
Which meant something important: he couldn’t use [Abyssal Slash] here.
At least, not without burning himself in the process.
"Fool... human!" the [Hellish Hobgoblin] let out a rough laugh, clearly amused by what it had just seen as it took another heavy step forward, its burning bat dragging slightly against the ground.
Leon didn’t even bother replying. There was no point wasting time.
Instead, he pushed forward again.
Even without [Abyssal Slash], his physical stats were still overwhelming, and with the [Power Sword] in his hand, every single attack he made carried double the strength it normally should have.
SLASH!
The remaining [Fire Hobgoblins], who had just regained their confidence thanks to their boss, rushed toward Leon all at once, believing they could overwhelm him with numbers.
They didn’t even last a second. With a single, clean swing of his sword, Leon cut through all of them in one motion.
His blade sliced through their bodies as if they were nothing more than paper, leaving them split in half as their bodies collapsed to the ground.
His expression didn’t change. It was effortless.
Even the [Hellish Hobgoblin] paused for a brief moment, clearly surprised by the sheer power behind that single attack.
But Leon didn’t give it time to react.
Fwoosh!
He closed the distance instantly before swinging his sword directly toward the boss.
The [Hellish Hobgoblin] responded immediately, raising its massive flaming bat and bringing it down with full force.
BOOM!
The clash shook the entire clearing, the impact sending shockwaves through the air as both of them held their ground, neither one stepping back despite the force behind the collision.
Leon narrowed his eyes slightly.
’Damn... even with double strength, that thing isn’t backing down easily,’ he thought as he adjusted his footing, ’Breaking its weapon is probably not happening either.’
Slash! Slash!
The two of them exchanged blows rapidly, their weapons colliding again and again, sparks and flames scattering around them as neither side showed any intention of retreating.
Leon pressed forward aggressively, aiming to end the fight as quickly as possible before the situation worsened.
But the boss... Every movement it made was calculated.
It focused on blocking, redirecting, and minimizing damage rather than rushing in blindly, which made it far more dangerous than Leon initially expected.
Blood Beam! Ice Spikes! Vines of Torment! Powerful Fireball!
Leon didn’t rely on just his sword.
He continuously cast spells in between attacks, launching them one after another in an attempt to overwhelm the boss from multiple angles.
But none of it worked the way he wanted.
The attacks were either blocked, tanked, or deflected.
’Holy hell... that thing is even tankier than the [Will of Nature],’ Leon thought, his expression tightening slightly.1
And just as he expected... [Celestial’s Might] didn’t activate.
Their [Combat Power] was too close. There was no advantage to be gained there.
Slash! Slash! Slash!
Leon gritted his teeth slightly as his attacks continued to be blocked, the [Hellish Hobgoblin] maintaining that same twisted grin as if it was enjoying the fight.
Then—
RUMBLE! RUMBLE!
The ground shook again. This time, much closer.
Leon’s eyes shifted for just a second. He knew time was running out.
If he didn’t end this quickly, things were going to get far worse.
Fwoosh!
Leon leaped forward with full force, closing the distance between him and the boss in an instant.
But this time... He didn’t swing his sword immediately.
Instead, something else happened.
A deep crimson aura began to gather around his blade, spreading outward and wrapping around his body as well, the energy intensifying with every passing second.
And when he was just a few meters away—
CRIMSON DANCE!
Leon swung his sword.
At first, it seemed like he didn’t hit anything as the blade cut through empty air.
For a split second, even the [Hellish Hobgoblin] seemed confused.
It reacted instantly, assuming Leon had made a mistake. It raised its bat and swung it down with full force.
Darkness Barrier!
Leon activated his defensive skill without hesitation, a barrier forming around him just in time.
BAM!
The impact hit him directly, the force pushing him slightly, but the barrier held.
And in that exact moment—
Slash! Slash! Slash!
Dozens of crimson slashes suddenly appeared around the [Hellish Hobgoblin], striking it from every direction at once as if invisible blades were cutting through its body repeatedly.
The boss had no time to react. It had committed to its attack. It couldn’t defend.
"GRRHHAAAAH!"
The [Hellish Hobgoblin] staggered backward, blood pouring from multiple deep wounds as its body shook under the accumulated damage.
Yet it didn’t fall. Even after all of that, it was still standing.
Leon let out a breath, "That thing is a goddamn tank..."
But at this point, it didn’t matter anymore. Because the rumbling had reached its peak.
Leon turned his head. And what he saw made him click his tongue slightly.
"Damn..."
From all directions, emerging from the burning forest and cracked ground, dozens upon dozens of enemies entered the clearing.
Groups of [Pyroman Apes] and [Fire Hobgoblins], all of them rushing in at the same time.
Leon was completely surrounded.
ROOOOAR!
The [Hellish Hobgoblin] roared once more. This time, it wasn’t just noise It was using a buff skill.
Small flames ignited around every monster in the clearing, their bodies glowing faintly as their strength increased, their eyes burning with intensity as they locked onto Leon.
Leon adjusted his stance slowly, gripping his weapon tightly.
’Those [Phoenix Wings] would’ve been really useful right now...’ he thought with a faint smile, despite the situation, ’Oh well.’
Running wasn’t an option. So there was only one thing left to do: fight.

The [Hellish Hobgoblin], heavily injured from the [Crimson Dance], stepped back slightly, choosing to stay at a distance now instead of engaging directly, clearly aware that another hit like that could be dangerous.
Instead, it let the others move forward.
[Fire Hobgoblin]
[Level: 75]
[Talent: Flame Affinity (C-Level)]
[Details: A group of hobgoblins that naturally evolved by staying in the "Hellish Beach"]
[Pyroman Ape]
The boost was clear. A flat increase of 50,000 [Combat Power] across the board.
That wasn’t something to ignore. But Leon didn’t look worried. Not even slightly.
’If I had a water-based skill, this would’ve been over instantly,’ he thought calmly, already planning ahead for the future, ’I’ll get one eventually.’
That was the advantage of mastering multiple elements, as it allowed him to be able to deal with elemental enemies like this.
Right now though, he would make do with what he had.
Leon stood there, surrounded from every direction, facing the injured boss and dozens of enhanced monsters at the same time.
And yet, he didn’t step back.

"Fool... human!" the [Hellish Hobgoblin] let out a rough laugh, clearly amused by what it had just seen as it took another heavy step forward, its burning bat dragging slightly against the ground.
Leon didn’t even bother replying.
There was no point wasting time.
Instead, he pushed forward again.
Even without [Abyssal Slash], his physical stats were still overwhelming, and with the [Power Sword] in his hand, every single attack he made carried double the strength it normally should have.
SLASH!
The remaining [Fire Hobgoblins], who had just regained their confidence thanks to their boss, rushed toward Leon all at once, believing they could overwhelm him with numbers.
They didn’t even last a second.
With a single, clean swing of his sword, Leon cut through all of them in one motion.
His blade sliced through their bodies as if they were nothing more than paper, leaving them split in half as their bodies collapsed to the ground.
His expression didn’t change.
It was effortless.
Even the [Hellish Hobgoblin] paused for a brief moment, clearly surprised by the sheer power behind that single attack.
But Leon didn’t give it time to react.
Fwoosh!
He closed the distance instantly before swinging his sword directly toward the boss.
The [Hellish Hobgoblin] responded immediately, raising its massive flaming bat and bringing it down with full force.
BOOM!
The clash shook the entire clearing, the impact sending shockwaves through the air as both of them held their ground, neither one stepping back despite the force behind the collision.
Leon narrowed his eyes slightly.
’Damn... even with double strength, that thing isn’t backing down easily,’ he thought as he adjusted his footing, ’Breaking its weapon is probably not happening either.’
Slash!
Slash!
The two of them exchanged blows rapidly, their weapons colliding again and again, sparks and flames scattering around them as neither side showed any intention of retreating.
Leon pressed forward aggressively, aiming to end the fight as quickly as possible before the situation worsened.
But the boss...
Every movement it made was calculated.
It focused on blocking, redirecting, and minimizing damage rather than rushing in blindly, which made it far more dangerous than Leon initially expected.
Blood Beam!
Ice Spikes!
Vines of Torment!
Powerful Fireball!
Leon didn’t rely on just his sword.
He continuously cast spells in between attacks, launching them one after another in an attempt to overwhelm the boss from multiple angles.
But none of it worked the way he wanted.
The attacks were either blocked, tanked, or deflected.
’Holy hell... that thing is even tankier than the [Will of Nature],’ Leon thought, his expression tightening slightly.1
And just as he expected...
[Celestial’s Might] didn’t activate.
Their [Combat Power] was too close.
There was no advantage to be gained there.
Slash!
Slash!
Slash!
Leon gritted his teeth slightly as his attacks continued to be blocked, the [Hellish Hobgoblin] maintaining that same twisted grin as if it was enjoying the fight.
Then—
RUMBLE!
RUMBLE!
The ground shook again.
This time, much closer.
Leon’s eyes shifted for just a second.
He knew time was running out.
If he didn’t end this quickly, things were going to get far worse.
Fwoosh!
Leon leaped forward with full force, closing the distance between him and the boss in an instant.
But this time...
He didn’t swing his sword immediately.
Instead, something else happened.
A deep crimson aura began to gather around his blade, spreading outward and wrapping around his body as well, the energy intensifying with every passing second.
And when he was just a few meters away—
CRIMSON DANCE!
Leon swung his sword.
At first, it seemed like he didn’t hit anything as the blade cut through empty air.
For a split second, even the [Hellish Hobgoblin] seemed confused.
It reacted instantly, assuming Leon had made a mistake.
It raised its bat and swung it down with full force.
Darkness Barrier!
Leon activated his defensive skill without hesitation, a barrier forming around him just in time.
BAM!
The impact hit him directly, the force pushing him slightly, but the barrier held.
And in that exact moment—
Slash!
Slash!
Slash!
Dozens of crimson slashes suddenly appeared around the [Hellish Hobgoblin], striking it from every direction at once as if invisible blades were cutting through its body repeatedly.
The boss had no time to react.
It had committed to its attack.
It couldn’t defend.
"GRRHHAAAAH!"
The [Hellish Hobgoblin] staggered backward, blood pouring from multiple deep wounds as its body shook under the accumulated damage.
Yet it didn’t fall.
Even after all of that, it was still standing.
Leon let out a breath, "That thing is a goddamn tank..."
But at this point, it didn’t matter anymore.
Because the rumbling had reached its peak.
Leon turned his head.
And what he saw made him click his tongue slightly.
"Damn..."
From all directions, emerging from the burning forest and cracked ground, dozens upon dozens of enemies entered the clearing.
Groups of [Pyroman Apes] and [Fire Hobgoblins], all of them rushing in at the same time.
Leon was completely surrounded.
ROOOOAR!
The [Hellish Hobgoblin] roared once more.
This time, it wasn’t just noise It was using a buff skill.
Small flames ignited around every monster in the clearing, their bodies glowing faintly as their strength increased, their eyes burning with intensity as they locked onto Leon.
Leon adjusted his stance slowly, gripping his weapon tightly.
’Those [Phoenix Wings] would’ve been really useful right now...’ he thought with a faint smile, despite the situation, ’Oh well.’
Running wasn’t an option.
So there was only one thing left to do: fight.

The [Hellish Hobgoblin], heavily injured from the [Crimson Dance], stepped back slightly, choosing to stay at a distance now instead of engaging directly, clearly aware that another hit like that could be dangerous.
Instead, it let the others move forward.
[Fire Hobgoblin]
[Level: 75]
[Talent: Flame Affinity (C-Level)]
[Details: A group of hobgoblins that naturally evolved by staying in the "Hellish Beach"]
[Pyroman Ape]
The boost was clear.
A flat increase of 50,000 [Combat Power] across the board.
That wasn’t something to ignore.
But Leon didn’t look worried.
Not even slightly.
’If I had a water-based skill, this would’ve been over instantly,’ he thought calmly, already planning ahead for the future, ’I’ll get one eventually.’
That was the advantage of mastering multiple elements, as it allowed him to be able to deal with elemental enemies like this.
Right now though, he would make do with what he had.
Leon stood there, surrounded from every direction, facing the injured boss and dozens of enhanced monsters at the same time.
And yet, he didn’t step back.

chapters.title: Chapter 193: The Hellish Hobgoblin’s Horde [3]
paragraphs: Surrounded from every side by the [Pyroman Apes], [Fire Hobgoblins], and the towering [Hellish Hobgoblin], Leon didn’t rush in blindly.
Instead he stood still for a brief moment, his eyes scanning the battlefield with calm precision as he took the time to properly assess everything around him.

’36 [Pyroman Apes] and 45 [Fire Hobgoblins],’ he thought, clearly more excited than intimidated by the situation he had found himself in, ’My inventory is definitely getting full after this, and [Celestial Hand] is probably going to trigger a few times.’
The idea of all the loot that would drop from such a large group of monsters was already enough to make this fight worth it in his eyes.
And considering that every single one of these creatures possessed some kind of sub-talent, the potential gains were even greater than usual.

’Celeste and Emilia are going to benefit a lot from this,’ Leon continued thinking as he slightly adjusted his grip on both his staff and sword, ’Especially if I can stack enough sub-talents for them... as for the essences and the rest, I’ll sort that out afterward.’
Before he could think any further, the monsters didn’t waste a single second.
Fwoosh!
As if they had all been given the same command at once, the entire group surged forward, flames flickering around their bodies as they charged toward Leon from every direction.
Their intent was clear as day: overwhelm him completely and crush him before he could react properly.

"Die... human," the [Hellish Hobgoblin] spoke once again from the back, its voice rough and filled with hostility as blood continued to drip from its mouth, clearly still affected by Leon’s previous attack, yet far from out of the fight.
At that exact moment, Leon briefly considered something extreme.
For a split second, the thought of using [Oblivion Meteor] crossed his mind.
It would have ended everything instantly, wiping out not only the monsters in front of him but potentially everything within a massive radius, leaving nothing behind.
But the downsides were far too significant to ignore.
First, the spell didn’t discriminate between enemies and allies, meaning Celeste and Emilia would be caught in it.
Second, and more importantly, Leon himself wasn’t immune to its power.
Using it right now would essentially be a suicide attack.
The only way he could safely rely on something like that was if [Life Vessel] was active, allowing him to revive afterward.
But since it was still on cooldown, that option was completely off the table.

And considering how his [Spirit] stat kept increasing, the destructive power of [Oblivion Meteor] would only grow stronger over time, potentially reaching a level where it could wipe out entire regions or even kingdoms.
’I don’t need that right now,’ Leon thought calmly, pushing the idea aside without hesitation.
Still, the thought lingered.

"I’ll get more [Forbidden Spells] eventually... and maybe even my first bloodline," he muttered under his breath, his eyes sharpening slightly as he focused back on the battle unfolding in front of him.
For now though, survival and efficiency were his only priorities.
Darkness Barrier!
A dark aura instantly formed around Leon, condensing into a protective barrier that surrounded his entire body, its surface faintly pulsing as it prepared to absorb incoming damage.

Even though his [Combat Power] was higher than most of the monsters charging at him, their sheer numbers and the buffs granted by the [Hellish Hobgoblin] meant that they were still capable of dealing real damage if he let them overwhelm him.
And Leon had no intention of letting that happen. A confident grin slowly appeared on his face.
"You’re about to find out exactly why mages stay at the top," he said calmly as he raised his staff, energy beginning to gather around him in multiple forms at once.
Then, without holding back even slightly—
Fwoosh!
Powerful Fireball! Torrent of Lightning! Blood Beam! Ice Spikes! Vines of Torment!
Leon unleashed everything at once.
A storm of magic erupted from his position, spreading outward in every direction as each spell took form, overlapping with the others to create complete chaos within the clearing.
If he had been relying purely on swordsmanship, fighting this many enemies at the same time would have been extremely difficult, if not outright impossible depending on the circumstances.
’Heh...’ Leon thought as a small, almost nostalgic smile appeared on his face, ’This is probably the closest I’ve been to THAT moment so far.’
He had experienced similar situations before, like when he faced the forces of the [Church of Light] or in [Labyrinth of Souls].
But this exact scenario, being completely surrounded by enemies with a stronger entity watching over them, felt eerily familiar.

Of course, these monsters were nothing compared to the beings he had once faced in his past life, especially not the [God of Eternity] and its followers, who could erase entire armies with a mere thought.
But still... the feeling was there.
And this time, Leon had no intention of being overwhelmed.
BOOM!
The [Powerful Fireball] exploded right in the middle of the charging horde, flames bursting outward in a violent wave as several monsters were caught directly in the blast.
Even though many of them possessed fire-related affinities, their resistance was nowhere near enough to withstand the sheer intensity of Leon’s attack.
Those caught at the center were instantly reduced to ash.
Zap! Zap! ZAP!
At the same time, bolts of lightning descended from above, striking multiple targets in rapid succession, the confined space making it nearly impossible for the monsters to dodge effectively.
Some were killed outright, while others were left stunned, their bodies twitching as electricity coursed through them.
And then—
Snap! Crack!

The [Vines of Torment] erupted from the ground once more, twisting and lashing out at anything within reach, their dark forms resisting the flames long enough to wrap around several enemies and crush them without mercy.
Some monsters attempted to burn the vines, launching fire attacks in desperation, but it took multiple hits just to weaken a single vine, and by then, the damage had already been done.
BAM! BOOM!
Spikes of ice shot up from the ground, impaling a handful of enemies before quickly beginning to melt under the intense heat of the environment.
’Ice and fire really are situational,’ Leon thought as he observed the effect, ’It’s too hot here for this to last long... but it still does the job.’
And finally—
BOOM!
The [Blood Beam] shot forward, carving a path through the remaining monsters, its raw force pushing them back while dealing heavy damage.
’I need to level up [Ice Spikes] and [Blood Beam] soon,’ Leon noted mentally, already planning ahead, ’They’re still lagging behind the others.’
Even at their current levels, they were still effective, but he knew they could become much stronger with the right investment.
Two [Pyroman Apes] managed to break through the barrage and close the distance, their torches swinging wildly as they aimed directly for Leon.
But—
Fwoosh!
Leon reacted instantly.
He turned his body slightly, redirecting the [Blood Beam] at one of them at point-blank range, completely erasing it from existence.
The second ape’s attack came in right after, but Leon stepped aside with precise timing, avoiding the strike before countering with his sword in one smooth motion.
SLASH!
The ape’s head fell to the ground before its body even realized what had happened.
Leon’s control over both his staff and sword was seamless, his movements flowing naturally despite the chaos around him.
Many players would struggle to manage both melee and magic simultaneously, especially under this kind of pressure.
But for Leon... it was second nature.
Still, he knew there was room for improvement.
’If I find a weapon that can combine both physical and magical output, that would be perfect,’ he thought, recalling the kind of equipment he had once used in his past life.
For now though, what he had was more than enough.
As the dust settled from his barrage of attacks, the battlefield had changed drastically.
Most of the monsters that had rushed him were already dead, their bodies scattered across the clearing.
Only around two dozen remained.
And for the first time... hesitation appeared in their movements.
They had seen what Leon could do.
They understood, at least on some level, that this human was far beyond anything they had faced before.
But before any of them could even think about retreating—
ROOOAR!
The [Hellish Hobgoblin] roared once again, its voice filled with authority and rage.
Its eyes locked onto the remaining monsters, forcing them into submission.
Even if they wanted to run, they couldn’t. Disobeying the boss would mean immediate death.
So their only choice was simple. Fight... or die.
Fwoosh!
With renewed desperation, the remaining monsters charged forward once again, flames burning brighter around their bodies as they prepared for one final assault against Leon.
And as Leon watched them come, his expression didn’t change in the slightest.
He simply tightened his grip on his weapons, his stance steady, his mind focused.

chapters.title: Chapter 194: Death of the Hellish Hobgoblin, Celeste is Here
paragraphs: After around a full minute of continuous fighting, where the remaining monsters threw everything they had at him in a desperate final attempt to overwhelm him, the result ended up being exactly what Leon had expected from the start.
Their last assault was completely useless.
One after another, the leftover [Pyroman Apes] and [Fire Hobgoblins] fell under Leon’s attacks, unable to keep up with the constant pressure of his spells and sword strikes.
Their numbers rapidly decreasing until there was nothing left standing in the clearing except for a single figure: the [Hellish Hobgoblin].
The boss slowly straightened its posture, its massive body still covered in wounds from Leon’s previous attacks.
Yet despite that, it lifted its flaming bat once more, its breathing heavy but steady enough to continue the fight.
Then, without warning—
Fwoosh!
It swung its weapon down with full force, aiming directly at Leon’s head.
Leon reacted instantly.

He raised his sword sideways, positioning it carefully to deflect the incoming strike rather than trying to tank it head-on, knowing very well that meeting that kind of raw power directly would be a mistake.
But the moment the two weapons collided—
BOOM!

A powerful shockwave spread through the clearing as the impact echoed loudly, and even though Leon managed to block the attack, the force behind it was far greater than he anticipated, forcing his body downward slightly as his feet dug into the scorched ground beneath him.
’Tch...’ Leon narrowed his eyes slightly as he held his ground, ’The double strength blessing doesn’t apply here... it only works when I’m attacking...’
That realization was annoying, but not unexpected.
If he wanted to take full advantage of his strength multiplier, he needed to be on the offensive, and right now, the boss was forcing him into a defensive position.
Before Leon could even adjust—
Fwoosh!
The [Hellish Hobgoblin] lifted its bat again and brought it down once more.
BOOM!
Another impact. Then again.
Fwoosh! BOOM!
And again.
The cycle repeated itself rapidly, the boss relentlessly attacking without giving Leon any time to breathe, each swing carrying enough power to crack the ground beneath them.
It was clear what it was trying to do: force Leon into a mistake and overwhelm him through sheer pressure.
But despite the intensity of the attacks, Leon didn’t panic.

He held his ground, carefully adjusting his stance with each impact, his muscles tightening as he absorbed the force and redirected it as best as he could, waiting for the right moment to strike back.
He knew that he couldn’t keep this up forever.
At some point, he would need to counterattack, even if it meant taking a hit in the process.

’I might have to drop the [Darkness Barrier] and just trade damage,’ Leon thought as he prepared himself mentally, his grip on his sword tightening slightly, ’As long as I can land a clean hit, this fight is over.’
He was ready to commit. But right as he was about to move—
Fwoosh!
A sudden blur cut through the air from beyond the clearing.
"GARGHHHHH!"
The [Hellish Hobgoblin] suddenly let out a roar of pain, its body jerking slightly as something struck it from the side.
Leon’s eyes widened as he instinctively looked up.
And what he saw immediately made him understand: Celeste. She had arrived.
Her figure was suspended mid-air, her [Phoenix Wings] spread wide behind her, glowing with a fiery brilliance that made her stand out against the burning environment around them.
The wings themselves were majestic, far larger than Pyra’s, yet clearly sharing the same origin.
Flames were dancing along their edges as they carried her effortlessly through the air.
Without hesitation, Celeste had used her speed and momentum to drive her spear directly into the side of the boss’s neck, managing to pierce through its defenses just enough to draw blood.
Of course, the attack wasn’t nearly strong enough to kill it.
Her [Combat Power] was still lower than the boss’s, and this kind of enemy couldn’t be taken down in a single strike by her alone.
But that didn’t matter. Because the moment she created that opening, it was already over.
While the [Hellish Hobgoblin] turned its attention toward Celeste, momentarily distracted by the unexpected attack, Leon didn’t waste even a fraction of a second.
Fwoosh!
He dashed forward instantly, closing the distance between them in the blink of an eye.
Crescent Slash!
Energy gathered at the tip of his blade as he swung it forward, releasing a sharp crescent-shaped attack that forced the boss to react.
Instinctively, the [Hellish Hobgoblin] raised its bat to block.
Exactly what Leon wanted. Because at that exact moment—
"Die."
Leon was already right in front of it.
SLASH!
His sword moved in a clean, precise arc.
The blade cut through the air... and then through the boss’s neck without resistance.
For a brief second, everything went silent.
Then—
Thud!
The massive body of the [Hellish Hobgoblin] collapsed to the ground, its head separated cleanly, its life extinguished instantly.
Ding!
[You have killed x40 "Pyroman Apes" and gained 1,300,000 experience points.]
[You have killed x49 "Fire Hobgoblin" and gained 1,960,000 experience points.]
[You have killed "Hellish Hobgoblin (Boss)" and gained 800,000 experience points.]
[100% Drop Rate has triggered...]
"Nice," Leon muttered with a small, satisfied smile as he lowered his sword slightly.
But right after—
Beep!
[Unfortunately, your "Storage Space" is full so the remaining items will drop on the corpses.]
"Yeah... I expected that," Leon sighed lightly.
With only 160 slots available in his [Storage Space], and many of them already occupied, it was obvious that defeating nearly a hundred monsters at once would exceed his capacity.
All around him, glowing items began to appear, scattered across the battlefield, shining brightly as they remained on the ground instead of being automatically stored.
Meanwhile, Celeste slowly descended from the air, her wings fading away as she landed in front of him, a small but satisfied smile on her face.
But the moment Leon looked at her properly, his expression changed: there was blood on her side.
"Oh shit," Leon said immediately as he stepped forward, his eyes narrowing slightly as he focused on the injury, "What happened?"
"I got clipped by one of the [Fire Hobgoblins] earlier," Celeste replied with a light smile, clearly trying to downplay it, "It’s nothing serious... my phoenix flames will heal it eventually."
Leon didn’t respond right away.
He simply looked at the wound for a few seconds, making sure it wasn’t anything critical, before finally nodding.
"Alright... just be careful," he said calmly, before shifting the topic, "By the way, how did you even find me?"
Celeste tilted her head slightly before answering.
"The monsters I was fighting suddenly stopped and rushed in this direction," she explained, "So I figured something big was happening here and followed them... I guess that worked out pretty well."
"Damn," Leon muttered.
That probably meant Emilia might also be heading this way. But for now, Leon turned his attention back to the battlefield.

It took him around ten full minutes to gather everything, moving from corpse to corpse, collecting the items that had dropped and placing them all together in one spot to properly evaluate what he had gained.
And when he finally finished, even he paused for a second.
I didn’t forget about the experience points or [Celestial Hand], it’s next Chapter.
